article.title: Frameworks
article.summary: The 18 frameworks available, including Indian financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA), how to turn them on, conditional requirements, and how to read a framework's status.

/frameworks.name: DPDP Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025
/frameworks.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
/frameworks.description: India's personal data protection law. Applies to digital personal data processed in India, and to processing outside India when it relates to offering goods or services to people in India. The Rules are phased in: Data Protection Board from 13 Nov 2025, Consent Manager provisions from 13 Nov 2026, and the remaining obligations from 13 May 2027.

/frameworks.name: CERT-In Directions (April 2022)
/frameworks.publisher: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY
/frameworks.description: Directions on information security practices, procedures, prevention, response and reporting of cyber incidents. Apply to service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations.

/frameworks.name: RBI Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, Resilience and Assurance Directions (2026)
/frameworks.description: The RBI's cybersecurity and IT governance rules for regulated entities, issued on 31 July 2026 as one Direction per entity type: commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, urban co-operative banks, NBFCs, credit information companies and all-India financial institutions. In force immediately, with no transition period. Replaces the 2023 IT Governance Master Direction and the 2016 Cyber Security Framework. Fintechs that serve these entities are asked to meet the same controls through their contracts.

/frameworks.name: RBI Digital Payment Security Controls Directions (2026)
/frameworks.description: Security controls for digital payment products and services of banks and credit-card issuing NBFCs: governance, secure application development, customer authentication, fraud risk, reconciliation, customer protection, and specific controls for internet banking, mobile payment apps and card payments. They also cover non-financial digital actions such as balance enquiry, PIN set and change, and mobile banking registration. Non-bank payment system operators follow the separate PSO Directions.

/frameworks.name: RBI Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for Non-bank PSOs (2024)
/frameworks.description: For authorised non-bank payment system operators: payment aggregators, prepaid payment instrument (wallet) issuers, card networks, ATM and white-label ATM operators, Bharat Bill Pay operating units, TReDS, cross-border money transfer operators and others. Large PSOs had to comply by 1 April 2025, medium ones by 1 April 2026 and small ones by 1 April 2028. PSOs must also make their payment gateways, technology providers and vendors follow these controls.

/frameworks.name: RBI Payment Aggregators Directions (2025)
/frameworks.description: For banks and non-banks acting as payment aggregators (online, physical point-of-sale and cross-border): the baseline technology recommendations, card data rules, data localisation, annual cyber security audit, merchant due diligence, escrow and dispute handling. Payment gateways are recommended to follow the same technology baseline. Non-bank PAs also follow the RBI cyber resilience Directions for non-bank PSOs.

/frameworks.name: RBI Digital Lending Directions (2025)
/frameworks.description: For banks, co-operative banks and NBFCs that lend digitally, and the lending service providers (LSPs) and digital lending apps (DLAs) that work for them. Covers borrower data, consent, storage in India, app permissions, the Key Fact Statement, cooling-off, grievance redressal, LSP due diligence and reporting of apps to RBI. The regulated entity stays accountable for anything it outsources to an LSP.

/frameworks.name: RBI Outsourcing of IT Services Directions (2023)
/frameworks.description: How banks, larger NBFCs, credit information companies and all-India financial institutions manage IT outsourcing and cloud. Fintechs and SaaS vendors serving them are not regulated directly, but these requirements are passed to them in contracts: due diligence, audit rights for the bank and RBI, data in India, approval of sub-contractors, fast incident notification, business continuity and exit.

/frameworks.name: SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF)
/frameworks.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
/frameworks.description: Replaces earlier SEBI cyber circulars for stock brokers, depository participants, mutual funds, AMCs, KRAs, RTAs, portfolio managers, AIFs and market infrastructure institutions. Organised by the NIST CSF functions plus "Evolve". Requirements scale with the RE category; ISO 27001 certification, the Cyber Capability Index and red teaming apply to MIIs and Qualified REs.

/frameworks.name: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines (2026)
/frameworks.publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
/frameworks.description: IRDAI's cyber security rules for insurers and insurance intermediaries (brokers, corporate agents, web aggregators, TPAs), updated in April 2026 to replace the 2023 guidelines and to require DPDP compliance. Insurance agents, point-of-sale persons and surveyors are covered through the insurer's minimum security framework.

/frameworks.name: IFSCA Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Guidelines (2025)
/frameworks.description: For entities licensed or registered by IFSCA in GIFT City (banks, fund managers, brokers, fintechs, insurers and others), applied in proportion to their size. Branches of regulated entities, entities serving only their group and entities with fewer than 10 employees can rely on their parent's framework for three years, with an annual certificate from the designated officer.

/frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
/frameworks.description: International standard for an Information Security Management System (ISMS). Certification requires the management system clauses (4 to 10) plus the applicable Annex A controls, justified in a Statement of Applicability.

/frameworks.name: SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria)
/frameworks.description: Attestation report on controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. Security (Common Criteria) is always in scope. Availability and Confidentiality are included by default; Processing Integrity and Privacy apply when you add them to your report scope (set this in your company profile).

/frameworks.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
/frameworks.publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
/frameworks.description: A voluntary framework of cybersecurity outcomes grouped into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. Widely used by US customers and as a common language for security programmes. SEBI's CSCRF is built on the same functions.

/frameworks.name: PCI DSS v4.0.1
/frameworks.description: Security standard for any organisation that stores, processes or transmits payment card data, or can affect its security. Required by card brands and acquiring banks; RBI's payment aggregator and tokenisation rules also lean on it. Requirements dated 31 March 2025 are now mandatory.

/frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI management system)
/frameworks.description: Certifiable standard for managing AI responsibly, for organisations that build, provide or use AI systems. Shares its management system structure with ISO 27001, so most governance controls carry over; the AI-specific controls cover impact assessment, data, lifecycle, transparency and suppliers.

/frameworks.name: EU GDPR (Regulation 2016/679)
/frameworks.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the EU
/frameworks.description: The EU's data protection law. Applies to organisations established in the EU, and to organisations outside the EU (including Indian companies) that offer goods or services to people in the EU or monitor their behaviour. Fines reach EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover.

/frameworks.name: HIPAA Security and Breach Notification Rules
/frameworks.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
/frameworks.description: US rules for protecting electronic protected health information (ePHI). Apply to covered entities (health plans, providers, clearinghouses) and to business associates that handle ePHI for them, which includes Indian health-tech, BPO and SaaS companies serving US healthcare customers.

article.title: Controls
article.summary: Working with controls - statuses, owners, bulk assignment, editing, custom controls, not applicable, and automation.

/controls.title: Access control policy
/controls.description: Define access control rules based on least privilege and need-to-know, covering systems that hold personal data.

/controls.title: Joiner, mover and leaver access process
/controls.description: Grant access on approved requests, adjust it on role change, and remove it within 24 hours of exit.

/controls.title: Multi-factor authentication
/controls.description: Enforce MFA for identity provider, cloud consoles, source code, email and all remote or administrative access.

/controls.title: Privileged access management
/controls.description: Limit admin and root access to named individuals, protect root accounts with MFA, and log privileged activity.

/controls.title: Periodic access reviews
/controls.description: Review user access to critical systems quarterly and remove access that is no longer needed.

/controls.title: Least privilege access to data
/controls.description: Restrict access to production data and personal data to roles that need it, enforced through role-based access.

/controls.title: Source code access
/controls.description: Restrict write and admin access to source code repositories and review it periodically.

/controls.title: Password and secrets management
/controls.description: Enforce strong password rules, use a password manager, keep secrets out of code, and scan repositories for leaked secrets.

/controls.title: Asset inventory
/controls.description: Maintain an inventory of hardware, software, cloud resources and information assets, each with an owner.

/controls.title: Acceptable use
/controls.description: Publish acceptable use rules for company systems and data, acknowledged by staff.

/controls.title: Information classification and handling
/controls.description: Classify information (for example Public, Internal, Confidential, Personal data) with labelling and handling and transfer rules for each level.

/controls.title: Media handling and secure disposal
/controls.description: Securely wipe or destroy media and equipment before disposal or re-use, and keep disposal certificates.

/controls.title: Endpoint security
/controls.description: Manage laptops and mobile devices with MDM, full-disk encryption, screen lock, OS updates and endpoint protection.

/controls.title: Protection of records
/controls.description: Protect business records from loss, tampering and unauthorised access, and keep them for the required retention periods.

/controls.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
/controls.description: Maintain a business continuity and DR plan with RTO and RPO targets, keep security in place during disruption, and test the plan annually.

/controls.title: Encryption at rest and key management
/controls.description: Encrypt databases, storage volumes, backups and object storage at rest, with managed keys and documented key rotation.

/controls.title: Cyber Crisis Management Plan
/controls.description: Keep a Board-approved Cyber Crisis Management Plan covering detection, containment, response and recovery for cyber scenarios, aligned with CERT-In guidance, tested through drills or tabletop exercises at least yearly.

/controls.title: Independent annual IS and cyber security audit
/controls.description: Have qualified, independent auditors (CERT-In empanelled where the regulator requires) audit information systems and cyber security at least yearly, report to the Board or its committee, submit reports to the regulator when required, and track findings to closure.

/controls.title: Customer authentication for payments and sensitive changes
/controls.description: Require multi-factor authentication (with at least one dynamic factor) for payments, new beneficiaries, limit changes and changes to contact details, use risk-based or adaptive checks, lock accounts after repeated failures and protect sessions against hijacking.

/controls.title: Customer transaction alerts
/controls.description: Alert customers instantly for every debit, credit and sensitive account change, show the actual merchant name, mask account and card numbers, and apply a cooling period after mobile number or email changes.

/controls.title: Transaction fraud monitoring and limits
/controls.description: Monitor transactions in real time with documented fraud rules (velocity, geo-location, device, high-risk merchants, failed authentications), set and review transaction limits, staff a 24x7 fraud desk, and analyse the root cause of frauds.

/controls.title: Mobile and web payment application security
/controls.description: Protect customer apps with device binding, detection of rooted or tampered devices and remote-access apps, obfuscation, encrypted local storage, no stored credentials, forced upgrades of old versions, server-side checks for genuine apps, and takedown of rogue apps and phishing sites.

/controls.title: Payment system data stored only in India
/controls.description: Store all payment system data (end-to-end transaction details and customer data collected for payments) only in India, delete any copy processed abroad within the permitted time, and report compliance (with a system audit) as RBI requires.

/controls.title: Customer protection and grievance redressal
/controls.description: Give customers secure-usage guidance, an easy in-app and web route to report fraud and raise complaints, a named grievance officer and escalation matrix, online dispute resolution and refund timelines, and disclose risks and charges before they sign up.

/controls.title: Payment reconciliation and settlement controls
/controls.description: Reconcile transactions with banks, networks and merchants daily (settlement files within 24 hours of receipt), keep customer funds in the designated escrow or nodal account with only permitted credits and debits, and resolve differences on time.

/controls.title: Merchant and partner onboarding due diligence
/controls.description: Verify merchants and partners before onboarding (KYC, background checks, security assessment of their integration), monitor their transactions against their business profile, and offboard those that breach requirements.

/controls.title: Regulator-mandated IT governance committees and CISO independence
/controls.description: Run the IT Strategy Committee, IT Steering Committee and Information Security Committee at the required frequency and composition, and keep the CISO independent of the Head of IT and free of business targets, reporting cyber risk to the Board or its committee at least quarterly.

/controls.title: Information security policy
/controls.description: Maintain a top-level information security policy approved by management, published to all staff and reviewed at least annually.

/controls.title: ISMS scope and context
/controls.description: Document the organisation's context, interested parties and their requirements, and the scope and boundaries of the security programme.

/controls.title: Leadership oversight and management review
/controls.description: Leadership reviews the security programme at least annually, covering performance, risks, audit results and improvements, and records decisions.

/controls.title: Security roles and responsibilities
/controls.description: Define and assign security and privacy roles (security lead, DPO or privacy contact, control owners) with a documented responsibility matrix.

/controls.title: Segregation of duties
/controls.description: Identify conflicting duties (for example, approving and deploying the same change) and separate them or add compensating review.

/controls.title: Security objectives, resources and planning
/controls.description: Set measurable security objectives with owners and deadlines, allocate resources, and plan changes to the programme.

/controls.title: Document control and operating procedures
/controls.description: Control security documents with versioning, approval and access rules, and document key operating procedures.

/controls.title: Code of conduct
/controls.description: Publish a code of conduct covering ethics and integrity, acknowledged by all staff at joining and annually.

/controls.title: Internal security communication
/controls.description: Communicate security policies, objectives, changes and how to raise concerns to staff through regular channels.

/controls.title: External security and privacy commitments
/controls.description: Communicate security commitments to customers and partners through terms, a trust page and contractual documents, and keep them consistent with practice.

/controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact
/controls.description: Keep a current list of authority contacts (CERT-In, Data Protection Board, sector regulator, police cyber cell), designate a CERT-In Point of Contact, and maintain memberships of security interest groups.

/controls.title: Legal and regulatory requirements register
/controls.description: Maintain a register of applicable laws, regulations and contractual obligations (DPDP, CERT-In, IT Act, sector rules, customer contracts) and of software licences.

/controls.title: Internal audit and compliance checks
/controls.description: Run an internal audit programme with impartial auditors, and periodically check compliance with security policies and standards.

/controls.title: Security metrics and monitoring of the programme
/controls.description: Define and track security metrics (open vulnerabilities, training completion, access review completion) and report them to leadership.

/controls.title: Corrective action and continual improvement
/controls.description: Track nonconformities and control failures to root cause and corrective action, and verify actions are effective.

/controls.title: Security in projects and change initiatives
/controls.description: Include a security and privacy review in project kick-off and in significant business changes.

/controls.title: Competence for security roles
/controls.description: Define required competence for security and privacy roles and keep records of qualifications and training.

/controls.title: Board-level oversight of IT and cyber risk
/controls.description: A board committee (or the board itself) oversees IT strategy and cyber risk, meets on a fixed schedule, reviews the cyber risk posture and major incidents, and records its decisions.

/controls.title: Background verification
/controls.description: Run background checks proportionate to the role before joining, in line with applicable law.

/controls.title: Employment terms and confidentiality agreements
/controls.description: Include security and confidentiality obligations in employment and contractor agreements, signed before access is granted.

/controls.title: Security and privacy awareness training
/controls.description: Train all staff on security and DPDP privacy obligations at joining and annually, with role-based training for engineers.

/controls.title: Disciplinary process
/controls.description: Maintain a communicated disciplinary process for security and privacy policy violations.

/controls.title: Offboarding and return of assets
/controls.description: On exit, recover devices and assets, revoke access, and remind leavers of ongoing confidentiality duties.

/controls.title: Remote working security
/controls.description: Define security rules for remote work (secure networks, device use, no printing of confidential data) and enforce them technically where possible.

/controls.title: Security event reporting by staff
/controls.description: Give staff a simple channel to report suspected incidents and phishing, and make sure reports are triaged.

/controls.title: Incident response plan
/controls.description: Maintain and test an incident response plan with roles, severity levels, triage, containment, communication and regulator reporting steps.

/controls.title: CERT-In reporting within 6 hours
/controls.description: Report reportable cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them, using the prescribed format, and keep proof of submission.

/controls.title: Personal data breach notification
/controls.description: On a personal data breach, inform affected Data Principals and the Data Protection Board without delay, and submit the detailed report to the Board within 72 hours.

/controls.title: Post-incident review
/controls.description: Run a post-incident review for significant incidents and track improvement actions.

/controls.title: Evidence preservation
/controls.description: Preserve logs and forensic evidence during incidents with chain of custody.

/controls.title: Financial regulator incident reporting
/controls.description: Report cyber incidents to your financial sector regulator within its deadline (RBI through DAKSH or the PSO format, SEBI, IRDAI or IFSCA, usually within 6 hours of detection), send follow-up and root-cause reports when due, and keep proof of every submission.

/controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India
/controls.description: Collect security and access logs from all ICT systems centrally, protect them from tampering, and retain them for at least one year within India (meets CERT-In 180 days and DPDP one year).

/controls.title: Security monitoring and alerting
/controls.description: Monitor logs and systems for suspicious activity with defined alerts, triage and escalation.

/controls.title: Clock synchronisation (NIC / NPL NTP)
/controls.description: Synchronise all system clocks to NTP sources traceable to NIC or NPL (for example time.nplindia.org or samay1.nic.in) so log timestamps are reliable.

/controls.title: Network security and segmentation
/controls.description: Restrict inbound access with firewalls or security groups, segment production from other networks, and block public exposure of storage and databases.

/controls.title: Encryption in transit
/controls.description: Encrypt data in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher for external and internal traffic carrying personal or confidential data.

/controls.title: Malware protection
/controls.description: Run endpoint protection or EDR on all laptops and servers, with alerts monitored.

/controls.title: Vulnerability management
/controls.description: Scan infrastructure, containers and dependencies for vulnerabilities and fix them within defined timelines (for example critical 15 days, high 30 days).

/controls.title: Penetration testing
/controls.description: Commission an independent penetration test at least annually (CERT-In empanelled auditor where required) and track findings to closure.

/controls.title: Secure configuration baselines
/controls.description: Apply hardened configuration baselines (for example CIS benchmarks) to cloud, servers and endpoints, control software installation, and detect drift.

/controls.title: Capacity management
/controls.description: Monitor capacity and performance with alerts and autoscaling to meet availability commitments.

/controls.title: Backups and restore testing
/controls.description: Back up critical data and systems automatically, encrypt and store backups separately, and test restores at least quarterly.

/controls.title: Redundancy and high availability
/controls.description: Design critical systems with redundancy (multi-AZ, failover) to meet availability targets.

/controls.title: Data masking and test data
/controls.description: Do not use real personal data in non-production environments unless masked or synthetic.

/controls.title: Data leakage prevention
/controls.description: Apply controls to prevent leakage of sensitive data, such as email and cloud storage sharing restrictions and DLP rules.

/controls.title: Web filtering
/controls.description: Block access to known malicious websites through DNS or endpoint filtering.

/controls.title: Cardholder data environment scope and segmentation
/controls.description: Document every system, network and process that stores, processes or transmits cardholder data or can affect its security, keep a data-flow diagram, segment the cardholder data environment and confirm the scope at least every 12 months.

/controls.title: Protection of stored account data
/controls.description: Keep stored card data to a minimum with a retention limit, never store sensitive authentication data after authorisation, mask PAN when displayed and render it unreadable wherever stored (tokenisation, truncation or strong encryption).

/controls.title: Approved Scanning Vendor and internal vulnerability scans
/controls.description: Run internal vulnerability scans and external scans by a PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor at least once every three months and after significant changes, and rescan until passing.

/controls.title: Physical access control
/controls.description: Protect offices and secure areas with perimeter controls, badge or biometric entry, visitor logs and monitoring. For cloud-hosted systems, rely on the provider's attestations.

/controls.title: Environmental protection and equipment maintenance
/controls.description: Protect equipment from fire, water, power and cabling threats, and maintain it. For cloud infrastructure, review the provider's attestation.

/controls.title: Clear desk and clear screen
/controls.description: Enforce automatic screen lock and clear desk rules for confidential information.

/controls.title: Personal data inventory (record of processing)
/controls.description: Maintain an inventory of personal data processing activities with data categories, purposes, lawful ground, systems, processors, retention and transfers.

/controls.title: Privacy notice
/controls.description: Publish a standalone, itemised privacy notice in English and relevant Scheduled languages, with links to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board, and notify pre-Act users.

/controls.title: Consent capture and records
/controls.description: Capture specific, informed consent through a clear affirmative action, limited to necessary data, and keep records of notice version, purpose and timestamp.

/controls.title: Consent withdrawal
/controls.description: Let users withdraw consent as easily as they gave it, and stop processing (including by processors) within a defined time.

/controls.title: Legitimate use register
/controls.description: For processing without consent, record which legitimate use under Section 7 applies and the justification.

/controls.title: Data accuracy
/controls.description: Keep personal data accurate and complete where used for decisions or disclosed, with ways for users to update it.

/controls.title: Retention and erasure
/controls.description: Define retention periods per purpose, erase data (and have processors erase it) when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn, and give 48 hours' notice before erasure where the Rules require.

/controls.title: DPO or privacy contact published
/controls.description: Publish the contact details of the DPO or designated privacy person on the website and app, and include them in every response to a Data Principal.

/controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling
/controls.description: Publish how to make requests, verify identity, and handle access, correction, erasure, nomination and grievance requests within the response time (maximum 90 days for grievances).

/controls.title: Cross-border transfer assessment
/controls.description: Track where personal data is stored and accessed outside India, check against restricted country notifications and sectoral localisation rules.

/controls.title: Privacy by design and organisational measures
/controls.description: Embed privacy review in product design and maintain organisational measures (owners, procedures, reviews) that make DPDP obligations work in practice.

/controls.title: Risk assessment
/controls.description: Assess security and privacy risks at least annually and on significant change, using a documented method with risk owners and acceptance criteria.

/controls.title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability
/controls.description: Decide treatment for each risk, maintain a Statement of Applicability, and track the treatment plan to completion with risk owner approval.

/controls.title: Fraud risk assessment
/controls.description: Consider fraud scenarios (misuse of access, false reporting, payment fraud) as part of the risk assessment.

/controls.title: Change impact assessment
/controls.description: Assess the security impact of significant changes to the business, technology or vendors before they happen.

/controls.title: Threat intelligence
/controls.description: Subscribe to threat feeds (for example CERT-In advisories) and act on relevant threats.

/controls.title: Secure development lifecycle
/controls.description: Define secure development rules, including security requirements, threat modelling for major features, and secure architecture principles.

/controls.title: Code review and branch protection
/controls.description: Require peer review and passing checks before merging to main branches, enforced through branch protection.

/controls.title: Automated security testing
/controls.description: Run dependency scanning, static analysis and secret scanning in CI, and fix findings by severity.

/controls.title: Environment separation
/controls.description: Separate development, staging and production environments and accounts, with restricted production access.

/controls.title: Change management
/controls.description: Track, test and approve changes to production, with emergency change procedures and rollback.

/controls.title: Outsourced development oversight
/controls.description: Apply the same security requirements, reviews and testing to code built by contractors and agencies.

/controls.title: Audit testing on production systems
/controls.description: Plan and approve audit and security tests on production systems to avoid disruption.

/controls.title: Vendor risk management
/controls.description: Keep a vendor inventory with risk tiers, assess vendors before onboarding and periodically by tier, and track their security posture.

/controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements
/controls.description: Sign contracts with security requirements and a data processing agreement before sharing personal data with a processor, including breach notice, erasure and security safeguard obligations.

/controls.title: Cloud service security
/controls.description: Define how cloud services are selected, configured, monitored and exited, including shared responsibility and data location.

/controls.title: Outsourcing register, sub-contracting and exit plans
/controls.description: Keep a register of all outsourcing arrangements with materiality and criticality, approve sub-contracting in advance, and keep a tested exit plan for each material arrangement so data can be returned or destroyed and the service moved without disruption.

/policies.body_md:
# Acceptable Use Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma
**Applies to:** All employees and contractors using Paisa Setu Fintech devices, accounts, networks or data.

## 1. Purpose

This policy explains how you may and may not use Paisa Setu Fintech systems and information.

## 2. General rules

1. Use company systems mainly for business purposes. Limited personal use is allowed if it does not affect work or security.
2. Use only company-approved tools to store or share company and customer data.
3. Never share your passwords or MFA codes. Use the company password manager.
4. Lock your screen when you step away. Devices lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity.
5. Keep devices updated and do not disable encryption, endpoint protection or MDM.
6. Do not install unlicensed or unapproved software.

## 3. Personal data and confidential information

1. Access personal data only when your role needs it.
2. Do not copy customer or employee personal data to personal devices, personal email or personal cloud storage.
3. Do not use real personal data for testing unless it is masked.
4. Do not paste confidential or personal data into public AI tools or websites unless the tool is approved.

## 4. Remote working

1. Work only on company-managed devices.
2. Avoid untrusted public Wi-Fi; use a mobile hotspot or company VPN where required.
3. Keep screens out of view of others and do not print confidential information at home.

## 5. Prohibited use

You must not use company systems to break the law, harass others, access content unrelated to work that creates security risk, attempt to bypass security controls, or access data you are not authorised to see.

## 6. Monitoring

Paisa Setu Fintech monitors its systems for security purposes, in line with applicable law and our employee privacy notice.

## 7. Acknowledgment

All staff acknowledge this policy when they join and once a year.

/policies.title: Access Control Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Access Control Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure that only authorised people have access to Paisa Setu Fintech systems and data, and only the access they need.

## 2. Principles

- **Least privilege:** grant the minimum access needed for the role.
- **Need to know:** access to personal data and confidential data is limited to roles that require it.
- **Unique accounts:** every person has their own account. Shared accounts are not allowed except documented service accounts.

## 3. Account lifecycle

1. **Joiners:** access is granted on an approved request from the manager, based on role.
2. **Movers:** access is reviewed and adjusted within 5 working days of a role change.
3. **Leavers:** all access is removed within 24 hours of exit. Devices are recovered.

## 4. Authentication

1. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for the identity provider, email, cloud consoles, source code hosting, and all administrative or remote access.
2. Passwords are at least 12 characters, not reused, and stored in the company password manager.
3. Secrets, API keys and credentials are never stored in source code. Repositories are scanned for leaked secrets.

## 5. Privileged access

1. Administrative access is limited to named individuals approved by the security lead.
2. Cloud root accounts are protected with hardware or app-based MFA and used only for break-glass tasks.
3. Privileged activity is logged.

## 6. Access reviews

Access to critical systems (cloud, production databases, identity provider, source code, systems holding personal data) is reviewed every quarter by system owners. Unneeded access is removed and the review is recorded.

## 7. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/policies.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure Paisa Setu Fintech can continue critical operations and recover systems after a disruption, while keeping information secure.

## 2. Recovery objectives

| System tier | Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Recovery Point Objective (RPO) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1: customer-facing production | 4 hours | 1 hour |
| Tier 2: internal business systems | 24 hours | 24 hours |
| Tier 3: other systems | 72 hours | 24 hours |

## 3. Backups

1. Production data is backed up automatically, encrypted, and stored in a separate account or region within India unless otherwise approved.
2. Restores are tested at least quarterly and results are recorded.

## 4. Continuity plan

The plan covers roles and contacts, decision criteria for invoking the plan, recovery procedures for Tier 1 systems, communication with customers and regulators, and how security controls are maintained during disruption.

## 5. Testing

The plan is tested at least annually through a tabletop or failover exercise. Findings are tracked to closure.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually and after any invocation of the plan.

/policies.title: Data Protection and Privacy Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Data Protection and Privacy Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out how Paisa Setu Fintech processes digital personal data in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) and the DPDP Rules, 2025, and other applicable privacy laws.

## 2. Principles

1. **Lawful ground:** we process personal data only with valid consent or for a legitimate use allowed by Section 7 of the DPDP Act.
2. **Notice:** we give a clear, itemised notice before or when asking for consent.
3. **Purpose limitation and minimisation:** we collect only the data needed for the stated purpose.
4. **Accuracy:** we keep personal data accurate and complete where it is used for decisions or shared.
5. **Storage limitation:** we erase personal data when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn, unless the law requires us to keep it.
6. **Security:** we protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards.
7. **Accountability:** we remain responsible for processing done by our vendors on our behalf.

## 3. Data inventory

The privacy contact maintains an inventory of all processing activities, including data categories, purposes, lawful ground, systems, processors, retention periods and transfers outside India. It is reviewed every 6 months and when new processing starts.

## 4. Consent

Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given through a clear affirmative action. Users can withdraw consent as easily as they gave it. We keep records of notice versions and consent.

## 5. Rights of Data Principals

We support the rights to access information, correction and erasure, grievance redressal and nomination. Requests are logged, identity is verified, and responses are sent within our internal target of 30 days and never later than 90 days for grievances. Every response includes our privacy contact details.

## 6. Children's data

Paisa Setu Fintech does not knowingly process children's personal data unless verifiable parental consent has been obtained. We do not track, behaviourally monitor or target advertising at children.

## 7. Processors and transfers

We share personal data with processors only under a contract that includes security and data protection obligations. Transfers outside India are recorded and checked against any restrictions notified by the Government and sector regulators.

## 8. Privacy contact

Paisa Setu Fintech's privacy contact or Data Protection Officer is published on our website and app.

## 9. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/policies.title: Data Retention and Disposal Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Data Retention and Disposal Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy defines how long Paisa Setu Fintech keeps information and how it is securely disposed of.

## 2. Retention schedule

| Information | Retention | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer personal data | While the account is active, then erased within 90 days unless legally required | DPDP Act s.8(7) |
| Security and access logs | At least 1 year, stored in India | DPDP Rules R.6(e); CERT-In Directions (v) requires 180 days |
| Incident records | 5 years | Internal requirement |
| Employee records | As required by labour and tax laws | Applicable law |
| Financial records | 8 years | Companies Act / Income Tax Act |
| Backups | 35 days rolling | Internal requirement |

Owners of each information type may set shorter periods where the purpose ends sooner.

## 3. Erasure

1. Personal data is erased when the purpose is complete, consent is withdrawn, or the retention period ends, unless the law requires us to keep it.
2. Where the DPDP Rules require, users are informed at least 48 hours before erasure.
3. Processors are instructed to erase data in the same way, and confirm erasure.

## 4. Secure disposal

1. Digital media is securely wiped or cryptographically erased before re-use or disposal.
2. Devices that cannot be wiped are physically destroyed by an approved vendor, who provides a certificate.
3. Paper records containing confidential or personal data are shredded.

## 5. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/policies.title: Incident Response Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Incident Response Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy defines how Paisa Setu Fintech detects, responds to, reports and learns from security incidents and personal data breaches.

## 2. Reporting by staff

Anyone who suspects a security incident, phishing attempt, lost device or data exposure must report it immediately to the security team through the incident channel. Do not investigate on your own or delete evidence.

## 3. Severity levels

| Level | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEV-1 | Confirmed breach of personal or customer data, or major outage | Database exposed publicly |
| SEV-2 | Likely compromise with limited impact | Compromised employee account |
| SEV-3 | Suspicious event needing investigation | Phishing email reported |

## 4. Response process

1. **Triage:** decide whether the event is an incident and assign severity and an incident lead.
2. **Contain:** limit the impact (revoke credentials, isolate systems).
3. **Preserve evidence:** keep logs and system images with a record of who handled them.
4. **Eradicate and recover:** remove the cause and restore services safely.
5. **Communicate:** keep leadership, affected customers and regulators informed as required.
6. **Review:** hold a post-incident review for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and track actions.

## 5. Regulatory reporting

| Authority | Trigger | Deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CERT-In | Incident types listed in Annexure I of the CERT-In Directions | Within 6 hours of noticing |
| Data Protection Board | Any personal data breach | Without delay; detailed report within 72 hours |
| Affected Data Principals | Any personal data breach affecting them | Without delay |
| Sector regulator (if applicable) | As per sector rules (for example RBI, SEBI) | As per sector rules |

The incident lead records the time the incident was noticed. The platform tracks each deadline from that time. The DPO or privacy contact approves notices to Data Principals and the Board.

## 6. Testing

The incident response plan is tested at least once a year through a tabletop exercise.

## 7. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually and after every SEV-1 incident.

/policies.title: Information Security Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Information Security Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma
**Applies to:** All employees, contractors and third parties with access to Paisa Setu Fintech information or systems.

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out how Paisa Setu Fintech protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the information it holds, including personal data of customers and employees. It is the top-level policy of our information security programme. Topic-specific policies support it.

## 2. Objectives

Paisa Setu Fintech commits to:

1. Protect customer and company information from unauthorised access, change or loss.
2. Meet legal, regulatory and contractual requirements, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its Rules, the CERT-In Directions of April 2022, and customer contracts.
3. Identify and treat information security risks on a regular basis.
4. Report and respond to security incidents quickly, including reporting to CERT-In within 6 hours and to the Data Protection Board as required.
5. Continually improve the information security programme.

Leadership sets measurable security objectives each year and reviews progress at least annually.

## 3. Roles and responsibilities

- **Leadership** approves this policy, provides resources and reviews the programme at least once a year.
- **Security lead** runs the programme, maintains policies, coordinates risk assessments and audits, and reports to leadership.
- **Privacy contact / Data Protection Officer** owns DPDP obligations, data principal requests and breach notifications.
- **Control owners** operate the controls assigned to them and keep evidence current.
- **All staff** follow security policies, complete training, and report suspected incidents immediately.

## 4. Policy framework

This policy is supported by topic-specific policies, including Acceptable Use, Access Control, Incident Response, Data Protection and Privacy, Data Retention, Vendor Management, and Business Continuity. All policies are reviewed at least annually and after significant change.

## 5. Compliance and exceptions

Compliance with security policies is checked through internal audits and automated monitoring. Exceptions must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, approved by the security lead and recorded with an expiry date. Violations may lead to disciplinary action.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least every 12 months by the security lead and approved by leadership.

/policies.title: Vendor Management Policy
/policies.body_md:
# Vendor Management Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure vendors who access Paisa Setu Fintech systems or data meet our security and data protection requirements.

## 2. Vendor inventory and tiers

All vendors are recorded in the vendor inventory with an owner and a risk tier:

| Tier | Criteria | Review frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | Processes customer personal data or is essential to service delivery | Annually |
| High | Accesses internal confidential data or production systems | Annually |
| Medium | Limited access to internal data | Every 2 years |
| Low | No access to data or systems | At onboarding only |

## 3. Onboarding

Before a Critical or High vendor is engaged:

1. The vendor completes a security questionnaire or provides an independent report (ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report).
2. The security lead reviews the results and records the decision.
3. A contract is signed with security requirements, breach notification duties, audit rights and, where personal data is shared, a Data Processing Agreement covering DPDP obligations.

## 4. Ongoing monitoring

Vendors are reassessed according to their tier. Significant changes, incidents or expiring certifications trigger a new review.

## 5. Offboarding

When a relationship ends, access is revoked and the vendor confirms return or erasure of Paisa Setu Fintech data.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/questionnaires.title: Standard security questionnaire (Full)
/questionnaires.description: A complete security due-diligence questionnaire for vendors that host, process or can access your confidential data or production systems. framework.name: CERT-In Directions (April 2022)
framework.description: Directions on information security practices, procedures, prevention, response and reporting of cyber incidents. Apply to service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates and government organisations.

requirements.title: Synchronise ICT system clocks
requirements.guidance: Connect to the NTP servers of the National Informatics Centre (NIC) or National Physical Laboratory (NPL), or to NTP servers traceable to them. Organisations across geographies may use other accurate sources if they do not deviate from NIC/NPL.

requirements.title: Report cyber incidents within 6 hours
requirements.guidance: Report the cyber incident types listed in Annexure I to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them or being notified of them.

requirements.title: Designate a Point of Contact for CERT-In
requirements.guidance: Designate a Point of Contact to interface with CERT-In and share their details in the prescribed format. Keep the details current.

controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact

requirements.title: Provide information and assistance when ordered
requirements.guidance: When CERT-In issues an order or direction, provide the requested information or assistance within the stated time.

controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact

requirements.title: Maintain ICT system logs for 180 days in India
requirements.guidance: Enable logs of all ICT systems and keep them securely for a rolling period of 180 days within Indian jurisdiction. Provide them to CERT-In with incident reports or when ordered.

controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Register subscriber information (data centres, VPS, cloud, VPN providers)
requirements.guidance: Data centres, VPS providers, cloud service providers and VPN providers must register accurate subscriber or customer information and keep it for 5 years or longer as required by law after cancellation or withdrawal of registration.

requirements.title: KYC and transaction records (virtual asset service providers)
requirements.guidance: Virtual asset service providers, exchanges and custodian wallet providers must keep KYC information and records of financial transactions for 5 years.

article.title: Frameworks
article.summary: The 18 frameworks available, including Indian financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA), how to turn them on, conditional requirements, and how to read a framework's status.

framework.name: DPDP Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025
framework.description: India's personal data protection law. Applies to digital personal data processed in India, and to processing outside India when it relates to offering goods or services to people in India. The Rules are phased in: Data Protection Board from 13 Nov 2025, Consent Manager provisions from 13 Nov 2026, and the remaining obligations from 13 May 2027.

requirements.title: Process personal data only on a lawful ground
requirements.guidance: Every processing activity must rely on either consent of the Data Principal or a legitimate use listed in Section 7. Record the ground for each activity in the data inventory.

requirements.title: Give notice when requesting consent
requirements.guidance: Before or at the time of asking for consent, give a notice describing the personal data, the purpose, how to exercise rights, and how to complain to the Data Protection Board.

requirements.title: Notice for consent obtained before the Act
requirements.guidance: Where consent was taken before the Act commenced, send a notice to those Data Principals as soon as reasonably practicable.

requirements.title: Notice available in English or a Scheduled language
requirements.guidance: Let the Data Principal read the notice and the consent request in English or in any language listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

requirements.title: Valid consent
requirements.guidance: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action, and limited to the personal data needed for the stated purpose.

requirements.title: Withdrawal of consent
requirements.guidance: Let Data Principals withdraw consent at any time, with ease comparable to giving it.

requirements.title: Stop processing after withdrawal
requirements.guidance: After consent is withdrawn, stop processing (and make processors stop) within a reasonable time, unless another legal basis applies.

requirements.title: Consent through a registered Consent Manager
requirements.guidance: Where Data Principals use a registered Consent Manager, accept and honour consent given, managed, reviewed or withdrawn through it.

requirements.title: Ability to prove notice and consent
requirements.guidance: The Data Fiduciary carries the burden of proving that notice was given and consent obtained. Keep consent records with notice version, timestamp and purpose.

requirements.title: Document reliance on legitimate uses
requirements.guidance: Where processing relies on a legitimate use (for example, data voluntarily provided for a specified purpose, employment purposes, legal obligation, medical emergency), document which use applies and why.

requirements.title: Accountability for all processing, including by processors
requirements.guidance: The Data Fiduciary remains responsible for compliance for processing it does and processing done on its behalf by Data Processors.

requirements.title: Engage processors only under a valid contract
requirements.guidance: Engage a Data Processor only under a valid contract, and only to provide goods or services to Data Principals.

controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

requirements.title: Accuracy and completeness of personal data
requirements.guidance: Ensure personal data is complete, accurate and consistent when it is used to make decisions affecting the Data Principal or is disclosed to another Data Fiduciary.

requirements.title: Appropriate technical and organisational measures
requirements.guidance: Implement technical and organisational measures that ensure effective observance of the Act and Rules.

controls.title: Privacy by design and organisational measures

requirements.title: Reasonable security safeguards
requirements.guidance: Protect personal data in your possession or control, including processing by processors, with reasonable security safeguards to prevent a personal data breach.

controls.title: Encryption at rest and key management
Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Breach intimation to the Board and affected Data Principals
requirements.guidance: In the event of a personal data breach, inform the Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal in the prescribed form and manner.

requirements.title: Erase data when no longer needed
requirements.guidance: Erase personal data (and have processors erase it) when consent is withdrawn or when the specified purpose is no longer being served, unless retention is legally required.

requirements.title: Deemed end of purpose after inactivity
requirements.guidance: For prescribed classes of Data Fiduciaries, the purpose is deemed no longer served if the Data Principal has not engaged within the prescribed period. Apply the inactivity periods in the Rules.

requirements.title: Publish contact details for data protection queries
requirements.guidance: Publish the business contact information of the Data Protection Officer (if applicable) or a person who can answer Data Principals' questions about processing.

requirements.title: Effective grievance redressal mechanism
requirements.guidance: Establish an effective mechanism to redress grievances of Data Principals.

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Verifiable parental consent for children
requirements.guidance: Obtain verifiable consent of the parent or lawful guardian before processing personal data of a child (under 18) or of a person with disability who has a lawful guardian.

requirements.title: No processing detrimental to a child's well-being
requirements.guidance: Do not process children's personal data in a way likely to cause any detrimental effect on the child's well-being.

requirements.title: No tracking, behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising of children
requirements.guidance: Do not track or behaviourally monitor children, or direct targeted advertising at them, except where exempted.

requirements.title: Appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India
requirements.guidance: A Significant Data Fiduciary must appoint a DPO based in India, responsible to the board, who is the point of contact for grievance redressal.

requirements.title: Appoint an independent data auditor
requirements.guidance: Appoint an independent data auditor to evaluate compliance with the Act.

requirements.title: Periodic Data Protection Impact Assessment and audit
requirements.guidance: Carry out periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and periodic audits, and other measures as prescribed.

requirements.title: Right to access information
requirements.guidance: On request, provide a summary of personal data processed and the processing activities, the identities of other Data Fiduciaries and Processors it was shared with, and other prescribed information.

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Right to correction and erasure
requirements.guidance: On request, correct, complete, update or erase personal data for which consent was given, unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or legally required.

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Right of grievance redressal
requirements.guidance: Data Principals can raise grievances with the Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager, which must respond within the prescribed period. They must exhaust this route before approaching the Board.

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Right to nominate
requirements.guidance: Allow Data Principals to nominate another person to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity.

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Respect restrictions on transfer outside India
requirements.guidance: Personal data may be transferred outside India except to countries the Central Government restricts by notification. Track destinations and monitor notifications. Sectoral rules (for example RBI) may impose stricter localisation.

requirements.title: Notice content and format
requirements.guidance: The notice must be understandable independently of other information, give an itemised description of personal data and the specified purpose, and include a link or means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain to the Board.

requirements.title: Working with registered Consent Managers
requirements.guidance: Where integrated with a Consent Manager, follow the registration conditions and obligations in the Rules and the First Schedule.

requirements.title: Encryption, obfuscation, masking or tokenisation
requirements.guidance: Secure personal data with appropriate measures such as encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens mapped to that data.

controls.title: Encryption at rest and key management

requirements.title: Access control over computer resources
requirements.guidance: Apply appropriate measures to control access to computer resources used for processing personal data.

requirements.title: Visibility of access through logs and monitoring
requirements.guidance: Keep visibility on access to personal data through logs, monitoring and review, so unauthorised access can be detected, investigated and remediated.

controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Continuity of processing and backups
requirements.guidance: Ensure continued processing if confidentiality, integrity or availability is compromised, for example through data backups.

requirements.title: Retain logs for at least one year
requirements.guidance: Retain logs and relevant personal data for at least one year for detecting and investigating unauthorised access, unless another law requires otherwise.

controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Security safeguards in processor contracts
requirements.guidance: Include provisions in contracts with Data Processors requiring them to take reasonable security safeguards.

controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

requirements.title: Technical and organisational measures for observance
requirements.guidance: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security safeguards are effectively observed.

controls.title: Privacy by design and organisational measures

requirements.title: Inform affected Data Principals without delay
requirements.guidance: On becoming aware of a breach, inform each affected Data Principal without delay in plain language, covering the nature and extent, likely consequences, mitigation taken, safety measures they can take, and a contact person.

requirements.title: Inform the Board without delay and within 72 hours in detail
requirements.guidance: Inform the Data Protection Board without delay, and within 72 hours of becoming aware (or a longer period allowed by the Board) submit details of the facts, mitigation, findings about the cause and the persons responsible, remedial measures and notifications made.

requirements.title: Erasure periods and advance notice of erasure
requirements.guidance: Apply the time periods in the Third Schedule for prescribed classes of Data Fiduciaries, and inform the Data Principal at least 48 hours before erasure so they can log in or engage to keep their data.

requirements.title: Contact details on website, app and in responses
requirements.guidance: Prominently publish the DPO's or designated person's business contact information on the website or app, and mention it in every response to a Data Principal's request.

requirements.title: Verifiable consent mechanism for parents
requirements.guidance: Adopt technical and organisational measures to verify that the person giving consent for a child is an identifiable adult, using reliable identity and age details or a virtual token.

requirements.title: Verify lawful guardians of persons with disability
requirements.guidance: Verify that a guardian giving consent for a person with disability is appointed by a court or designated authority under applicable law.

requirements.title: Annual DPIA and audit, algorithm due diligence
requirements.guidance: Once every twelve months, carry out a DPIA and an audit and furnish the significant observations to the Board. Verify that algorithmic software is not likely to risk Data Principals' rights. Follow any data localisation directions issued for specified data.

requirements.title: Publish how to exercise rights; resolve grievances within 90 days

controls.title: Data principal rights and grievance handling

requirements.title: Meet Central Government requirements for transfers abroad
