framework.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
framework.description: International standard for an Information Security Management System (ISMS). Certification requires the management system clauses (4 to 10) plus the applicable Annex A controls, justified in a Statement of Applicability.

requirements.title: Understanding the organisation and its context
requirements.guidance: List internal and external issues that affect your ability to achieve ISMS outcomes.

requirements.title: Needs of interested parties
requirements.guidance: Identify customers, regulators, staff and others, their security requirements, and which you will address.

requirements.title: ISMS scope
requirements.guidance: Document the scope: locations, teams, products, systems and interfaces covered by the ISMS.

requirements.title: Information security management system
requirements.guidance: Establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the ISMS and its processes.

requirements.title: Leadership and commitment
requirements.guidance: Top management shows commitment: approves policy and objectives, provides resources, and reviews performance.

requirements.title: Information security policy
requirements.guidance: Publish a top-level security policy that includes objectives and a commitment to meet requirements and improve.

requirements.title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
requirements.guidance: Assign and communicate ISMS responsibilities, including who reports ISMS performance to management.

requirements.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities
requirements.guidance: Plan how the ISMS addresses risks and opportunities identified from context and interested parties.

requirements.title: Information security risk assessment
requirements.guidance: Define and apply a repeatable risk assessment method with risk owners and acceptance criteria.

requirements.title: Information security risk treatment
requirements.guidance: Choose treatment options, compare controls with Annex A, produce a Statement of Applicability and a treatment plan approved by risk owners.

controls.title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability

requirements.title: Information security objectives
requirements.guidance: Set measurable security objectives with owners, resources and deadlines.

requirements.title: Planning of changes
requirements.guidance: Make changes to the ISMS in a planned way.

requirements.title: Resources
requirements.guidance: Provide people, budget and tools needed for the ISMS.

requirements.title: Competence
requirements.guidance: Define required competence for ISMS roles and keep evidence of it.

requirements.title: Awareness
requirements.guidance: Staff know the policy, their contribution, and the consequences of not following requirements.

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.guidance: Decide what, when, with whom and how to communicate about security, internally and externally.

requirements.title: Documented information: general
requirements.guidance: Keep the documented information the standard and your ISMS need.

requirements.title: Creating and updating documents
requirements.guidance: Documents have identification, review and approval.

requirements.title: Control of documented information
requirements.guidance: Control distribution, access, storage, version and retention of documents.

requirements.title: Operational planning and control
requirements.guidance: Plan and control the processes that meet security requirements, including outsourced processes and changes.

requirements.title: Information security risk assessment (performed)
requirements.guidance: Run risk assessments at planned intervals and on significant change, and keep the results.

requirements.title: Information security risk treatment (performed)
requirements.guidance: Implement the risk treatment plan and keep the results.

controls.title: Risk treatment and Statement of Applicability

requirements.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
requirements.guidance: Decide what to measure, how and when, and evaluate ISMS effectiveness.

controls.title: Security metrics and monitoring of the programme

requirements.title: Internal audit: general
requirements.guidance: Run internal audits at planned intervals to check the ISMS conforms and is effective.

requirements.title: Internal audit programme
requirements.guidance: Plan the audit programme with criteria, scope, impartial auditors and reporting to management.

requirements.title: Management review: general
requirements.guidance: Top management reviews the ISMS at planned intervals.

requirements.title: Management review inputs
requirements.guidance: Cover previous actions, changes, performance, feedback, risk results and improvement opportunities.

requirements.title: Management review results
requirements.guidance: Record decisions on improvements and changes to the ISMS.

requirements.title: Continual improvement
requirements.guidance: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS.

requirements.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
requirements.guidance: React to nonconformities, find root causes, take corrective action and keep records.

requirements.title: Policies for information security
requirements.guidance: Approved, published, communicated and reviewed security policies and topic-specific policies.

requirements.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
requirements.guidance: Define and allocate security roles.

requirements.title: Segregation of duties
requirements.guidance: Separate conflicting duties to reduce fraud and error.

requirements.title: Management responsibilities
requirements.guidance: Managers require staff and contractors to follow security policies.

requirements.title: Contact with authorities
requirements.guidance: Maintain contacts with regulators and authorities such as CERT-In and law enforcement.

controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact

requirements.title: Contact with special interest groups
requirements.guidance: Maintain contacts with security forums and professional groups.

controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact

requirements.title: Threat intelligence
requirements.guidance: Collect and analyse threat information relevant to your organisation.

requirements.title: Information security in project management
requirements.guidance: Integrate security into project management.

controls.title: Security in projects and change initiatives

requirements.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
requirements.guidance: Maintain an inventory of information and assets with owners.

requirements.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
requirements.guidance: Document rules for acceptable use.

requirements.title: Return of assets
requirements.guidance: Recover organisational assets when employment or contracts end.

requirements.title: Classification of information
requirements.guidance: Classify information by confidentiality, integrity, availability and legal needs.

requirements.title: Labelling of information
requirements.guidance: Label information according to its classification.

requirements.title: Information transfer
requirements.guidance: Have rules and agreements for transferring information internally and externally.

requirements.title: Access control
requirements.guidance: Define access control rules based on business and security requirements.

requirements.title: Identity management
requirements.guidance: Manage the full lifecycle of identities.

controls.title: Joiner, mover and leaver access process

requirements.title: Authentication information
requirements.guidance: Control allocation and management of passwords and other authentication information.

requirements.title: Access rights
requirements.guidance: Provision, review, modify and remove access rights according to policy.

controls.title: Joiner, mover and leaver access process

requirements.title: Information security in supplier relationships
requirements.guidance: Manage security risks from suppliers' products and services.

requirements.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
requirements.guidance: Agree security requirements with each supplier in contracts.

controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

requirements.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
requirements.guidance: Manage security risks in the ICT product and service supply chain.

controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

requirements.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
requirements.guidance: Monitor and review supplier security and manage changes.

requirements.title: Information security for use of cloud services
requirements.guidance: Define how cloud services are acquired, used, managed and exited.

requirements.title: Incident management planning and preparation
requirements.guidance: Plan incident management with defined processes, roles and responsibilities.

requirements.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
requirements.guidance: Assess events and decide whether they are incidents.

requirements.title: Response to information security incidents
requirements.guidance: Respond to incidents according to documented procedures.

requirements.title: Learning from information security incidents
requirements.guidance: Use lessons from incidents to strengthen controls.

requirements.title: Collection of evidence
requirements.guidance: Identify, collect and preserve evidence related to security events.

requirements.title: Information security during disruption
requirements.guidance: Maintain security at an appropriate level during disruption.

requirements.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
requirements.guidance: Plan, implement, maintain and test ICT readiness for continuity objectives.

requirements.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
requirements.guidance: Identify and keep current your legal, regulatory and contractual security requirements.

requirements.title: Intellectual property rights
requirements.guidance: Protect intellectual property rights, including software licensing.

requirements.title: Protection of records
requirements.guidance: Protect records from loss, destruction, falsification and unauthorised access or release.

requirements.title: Privacy and protection of PII
requirements.guidance: Meet privacy and personal data protection requirements, including DPDP.

controls.title: Privacy by design and organisational measures

requirements.title: Independent review of information security
requirements.guidance: Have the security approach reviewed independently at planned intervals or on major change.

requirements.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards
requirements.guidance: Regularly check compliance with security policies and standards.

requirements.title: Documented operating procedures
requirements.guidance: Document operating procedures and make them available to those who need them.

requirements.title: Screening
requirements.guidance: Run background verification checks proportionate to the role and the law.

requirements.title: Terms and conditions of employment
requirements.guidance: Employment contracts state security responsibilities.

requirements.title: Information security awareness, education and training
requirements.guidance: Provide regular, role-appropriate security training.

requirements.title: Disciplinary process
requirements.guidance: Have a communicated disciplinary process for policy violations.

requirements.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
requirements.guidance: Security duties that remain after leaving are defined and communicated.

requirements.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
requirements.guidance: Use NDAs that reflect your protection needs, reviewed regularly.

requirements.title: Remote working
requirements.guidance: Protect information accessed or processed when working remotely.

requirements.title: Information security event reporting
requirements.guidance: Give staff a clear way to report security events quickly.

requirements.title: Physical security perimeters
requirements.guidance: Define perimeters protecting areas with information and assets.

requirements.title: Physical entry
requirements.guidance: Protect secure areas with entry controls.

requirements.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
requirements.guidance: Design and implement physical security for offices and facilities.

requirements.title: Physical security monitoring
requirements.guidance: Monitor premises for unauthorised physical access.

requirements.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
requirements.guidance: Protect against fire, flood, power and other physical threats.

requirements.title: Working in secure areas
requirements.guidance: Define rules for working in secure areas.

requirements.title: Clear desk and clear screen
requirements.guidance: Enforce clear desk and clear screen rules.

requirements.title: Equipment siting and protection
requirements.guidance: Site and protect equipment securely.

requirements.title: Security of assets off-premises
requirements.guidance: Protect laptops and other assets used outside the office.

requirements.title: Storage media
requirements.guidance: Manage storage media through acquisition, use, transport and disposal.

requirements.title: Supporting utilities
requirements.guidance: Protect against power and other utility failures.

requirements.title: Cabling security
requirements.guidance: Protect power and data cabling from interception and damage.

requirements.title: Equipment maintenance
requirements.guidance: Maintain equipment correctly.

requirements.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
requirements.guidance: Wipe or destroy data before disposing of or re-using equipment.

requirements.title: User endpoint devices
requirements.guidance: Protect information on laptops and mobile devices.

requirements.title: Privileged access rights
requirements.guidance: Restrict and manage privileged access.

requirements.title: Information access restriction
requirements.guidance: Restrict access to information according to the access control policy.

requirements.title: Access to source code
requirements.guidance: Manage read and write access to source code and development tools.

requirements.title: Secure authentication
requirements.guidance: Use secure authentication such as MFA based on access restrictions.

requirements.title: Capacity management
requirements.guidance: Monitor and adjust resources to meet capacity needs.

requirements.title: Protection against malware
requirements.guidance: Protect against malware, supported by user awareness.

requirements.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
requirements.guidance: Find, evaluate and fix technical vulnerabilities in a timely way.

requirements.title: Configuration management
requirements.guidance: Define, implement and monitor secure configurations.

requirements.title: Information deletion
requirements.guidance: Delete information when no longer required.

requirements.title: Data masking
requirements.guidance: Mask data according to access policy and legal requirements.

requirements.title: Data leakage prevention
requirements.guidance: Apply measures to prevent data leakage.

requirements.title: Information backup
requirements.guidance: Back up information and test restores regularly.

requirements.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
requirements.guidance: Build enough redundancy to meet availability requirements.

requirements.title: Logging
requirements.guidance: Produce, store, protect and analyse logs of activities and events.

controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Monitoring activities
requirements.guidance: Monitor networks and systems for anomalous behaviour and act on it.

requirements.title: Clock synchronisation
requirements.guidance: Synchronise system clocks to approved time sources.

requirements.title: Use of privileged utility programs
requirements.guidance: Restrict and control utilities that can override system controls.

requirements.title: Installation of software on operational systems
requirements.guidance: Control software installation on production systems.

requirements.title: Networks security
requirements.guidance: Secure, manage and control networks and devices.

requirements.title: Security of network services
requirements.guidance: Define and monitor security of network services.

requirements.title: Segregation of networks
requirements.guidance: Segregate groups of services, users and systems on networks.

requirements.title: Web filtering
requirements.guidance: Manage access to external websites to reduce exposure to malicious content.

requirements.title: Use of cryptography
requirements.guidance: Define and apply rules for cryptography and key management.

requirements.title: Secure development life cycle
requirements.guidance: Establish rules for secure development of software and systems.

requirements.title: Application security requirements
requirements.guidance: Identify and approve security requirements when building or buying applications.

requirements.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
requirements.guidance: Document and apply secure engineering principles.

requirements.title: Secure coding
requirements.guidance: Apply secure coding principles.

requirements.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
requirements.guidance: Define and run security testing in the development lifecycle.

requirements.title: Outsourced development
requirements.guidance: Direct, monitor and review outsourced development.

requirements.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
requirements.guidance: Separate and secure development, test and production environments.

requirements.title: Change management
requirements.guidance: Control changes to systems and facilities through change management.

requirements.title: Test information
requirements.guidance: Select, protect and manage test data appropriately.

requirements.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
requirements.guidance: Plan audit tests on operational systems to minimise disruption.

article.title: Frameworks
article.summary: The 18 frameworks available, including Indian financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA), how to turn them on, conditional requirements, and how to read a framework's status.

framework.name: RBI Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for Non-bank PSOs (2024)
framework.description: For authorised non-bank payment system operators: payment aggregators, prepaid payment instrument (wallet) issuers, card networks, ATM and white-label ATM operators, Bharat Bill Pay operating units, TReDS, cross-border money transfer operators and others. Large PSOs had to comply by 1 April 2025, medium ones by 1 April 2026 and small ones by 1 April 2028. PSOs must also make their payment gateways, technology providers and vendors follow these controls.

requirements.title: Extend controls to ecosystem partners
requirements.guidance: Make unregulated entities in your payment chain (payment gateways, technology providers, vendors) follow these Directions through agreements and a Board-approved policy.

controls.title: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

requirements.title: Board oversight and IT sub-committee
requirements.guidance: The Board oversees information security and cyber risk; it may delegate to a sub-committee headed by a member with security experience, meeting at least quarterly.

controls.title: Regulator-mandated IT governance committees and CISO independence
Board-level oversight of IT and cyber risk

requirements.title: Board-approved information security policy
requirements.guidance: An information security policy covering roles, risk identification and management and training, reviewed annually.

requirements.title: Board-approved Cyber Crisis Management Plan
requirements.guidance: A separate Cyber Crisis Management Plan, referring to CERT-In, NCIIPC and IDRBT guidance.

requirements.title: Accountable senior executive (CISO)
requirements.guidance: A senior executive with security expertise, such as a CISO, is accountable for the policy and the cyber resilience framework.

requirements.title: KRIs, KPIs and reporting of assessments
requirements.guidance: Define key risk and performance indicators monitored by the Board sub-committee, and table audit and VA/PT reports at its next meeting.

controls.title: Security metrics and monitoring of the programme

requirements.title: Cyber risk assessment before launches and major changes
requirements.guidance: Assess cyber risk before launching products or making major changes.

requirements.title: Asset inventory, data flows and end-of-life tracking
requirements.guidance: Keep asset registers and data-flow diagrams and track end of support.

requirements.title: Identity and access management
requirements.guidance: Least privilege, MFA for privileged accounts, default credentials changed before go-live, session timeouts and removable media controls.

requirements.title: Network security, SOC and SIEM
requirements.guidance: A SOC with SIEM correlation, anti-malware, layered boundary defences, segmentation and device checks before network access.

requirements.title: Application lifecycle security
requirements.guidance: Secure SDLC, database layer segregated from other tiers, and source code (or escrow) for critical procured applications.

requirements.title: Code review, VA and PT at least annually and before deployment
requirements.guidance: Source code review, VA and PT at least annually in authenticated mode, vendor certificates for code you don't own, security audit before any deployment, and recurring findings reported to the sub-committee.

requirements.title: Vendor risk and independent assurance
requirements.guidance: Manage vendor risk under the outsourcing framework, protect against infiltration from vendor environments, and get independent assurance for vendors in critical processes.

controls.title: Outsourcing register, sub-contracting and exit plans

requirements.title: Payment data stored in India
requirements.guidance: Comply with the RBI requirement to store payment system data only in India (circular of 6 April 2018).

controls.title: Payment system data stored only in India

requirements.title: Data security, PCI DSS and half-yearly restore tests
requirements.guidance: Data leak prevention, an ISMS, encryption in transit and at rest, PCI DSS for stored card data, and backup restore tests at least half-yearly.

controls.title: Encryption at rest and key management

requirements.title: Patch and change management
requirements.guidance: Apply critical patches immediately and test changes outside production first.

requirements.title: Report incidents to RBI within 6 hours
requirements.guidance: A Board-approved incident response mechanism with forensics; report incidents to RBI in the Annex 1 format within 6 hours of detection, and to CERT-In.

requirements.title: BCP, DR in another seismic zone, half-yearly drills
requirements.guidance: Scenario-based BCP reviewed annually, RTO/RPO aligned (near-zero RPO aspired), DR site in a different seismic zone, DR drills at least half-yearly.

requirements.title: API security
requirements.guidance: Authenticate and authorise API calls, protect message integrity and availability, and detect anomalies.

requirements.title: Training with minimum scores
requirements.guidance: Periodic training for employees and vendors; restrict access for staff below a benchmark score.

requirements.title: Cloud policy and annual CSP audit
requirements.guidance: A cloud operation policy, data segregation and annual independent audit of cloud providers.

requirements.title: MFA for debits, real-time fraud monitoring, 24x7 desk, 5-year logs
requirements.guidance: MFA for electronic debits unless relaxed, real-time fraud monitoring, a manned 24x7x365 desk for fraud complaints and law enforcement, audit logs kept at least five years, anti-phishing and rogue-app takedown.

controls.title: Customer authentication for payments and sensitive changes
Mobile and web payment application security
Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Risk alerts, masked notifications and fraud flagging
requirements.guidance: Online alerts on failed transactions, velocity and geo-location; masked account and card details; merchant name (not the gateway) in messages with the OTP at the end; customers can flag fraud in the app or website.

requirements.title: Mobile app controls and 12-hour cooling period
requirements.guidance: Device binding and re-binding after long non-use, inactivity timeout, lockout after failed logins, block while remote-access apps run, and a 12-hour cooling period after a mobile number or email change.

controls.title: Customer authentication for payments and sensitive changes
Mobile and web payment application security

requirements.title: Validated terminals, network limits and 24x7 alerts
requirements.guidance: PCI P2PE and PTS validated terminals, network-level transaction limits and 24x7x365 suspicious-activity alerts to issuers.

requirements.title: PPI alerts in local language and load cooling period
requirements.guidance: OTPs and alerts in the customer's language, and a cooling period before transfers or withdrawals after loading.

requirements.title: Cyber resilience Directions for non-bank PSOs
requirements.guidance: Non-bank PAs also follow the cyber resilience and digital payment security Directions for non-bank PSOs (30 July 2024).

requirements.title: Refunds to the original payment method

controls.title: Contact with authorities, CERT-In point of contact

requirements.guidance: Assess security risks and present them and audit reports to the Board.

controls.title: Board-level oversight of IT and cyber risk

requirements.title: Report security incidents and card data breaches to RBI
requirements.guidance: Report security incidents and card data breaches to RBI in the stipulated time, plus monthly cyber incident reports with root cause and preventive actions.

requirements.title: Security assessment of merchants at onboarding
requirements.guidance: Assess merchants' security during onboarding.

controls.title: Merchant and partner onboarding due diligence

requirements.title: Internal audits, external audit, half-yearly VAPT and PCI reports
requirements.guidance: Quarterly internal and annual external audit reports to the IT committee, half-yearly VAPT, and PCI DSS AOC or ROC.

controls.title: Approved Scanning Vendor and internal vulnerability scans

requirements.title: Annual review of the information security policy
requirements.guidance: Review the information security policy at least annually.

requirements.title: Cyber Crisis Management Plan
requirements.guidance: A Cyber Crisis Management Plan approved by the IT strategy committee.

requirements.title: Security event collection and analysis
requirements.guidance: Collect and analyse security events to raise alerts proactively.

controls.title: Centralised logging with retention in India

requirements.title: Data kept out of external jurisdictions
requirements.guidance: Take preventive measures so data is stored in infrastructure that is not in external jurisdictions.

controls.title: Payment system data stored only in India

requirements.guidance: Card credentials must not be stored in databases or servers that merchants can access; use tokenisation.

# Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure Paisa Setu Fintech can continue critical operations and recover systems after a disruption, while keeping information secure.

## 2. Recovery objectives

| System tier | Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Recovery Point Objective (RPO) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1: customer-facing production | 4 hours | 1 hour |
| Tier 2: internal business systems | 24 hours | 24 hours |
| Tier 3: other systems | 72 hours | 24 hours |

## 3. Backups

1. Production data is backed up automatically, encrypted, and stored in a separate account or region within India unless otherwise approved.
2. Restores are tested at least quarterly and results are recorded.

## 4. Continuity plan

The plan covers roles and contacts, decision criteria for invoking the plan, recovery procedures for Tier 1 systems, communication with customers and regulators, and how security controls are maintained during disruption.

## 5. Testing

The plan is tested at least annually through a tabletop or failover exercise. Findings are tracked to closure.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually and after any invocation of the plan.

# Access Control Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure that only authorised people have access to Paisa Setu Fintech systems and data, and only the access they need.

## 2. Principles

- **Least privilege:** grant the minimum access needed for the role.
- **Need to know:** access to personal data and confidential data is limited to roles that require it.
- **Unique accounts:** every person has their own account. Shared accounts are not allowed except documented service accounts.

## 3. Account lifecycle

1. **Joiners:** access is granted on an approved request from the manager, based on role.
2. **Movers:** access is reviewed and adjusted within 5 working days of a role change.
3. **Leavers:** all access is removed within 24 hours of exit. Devices are recovered.

## 4. Authentication

1. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for the identity provider, email, cloud consoles, source code hosting, and all administrative or remote access.
2. Passwords are at least 12 characters, not reused, and stored in the company password manager.
3. Secrets, API keys and credentials are never stored in source code. Repositories are scanned for leaked secrets.

## 5. Privileged access

1. Administrative access is limited to named individuals approved by the security lead.
2. Cloud root accounts are protected with hardware or app-based MFA and used only for break-glass tasks.
3. Privileged activity is logged.

## 6. Access reviews

Access to critical systems (cloud, production databases, identity provider, source code, systems holding personal data) is reviewed every quarter by system owners. Unneeded access is removed and the review is recorded.

## 7. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/policies/4dab17a5-e846-45ba-84cc-b12fe9.body_md:
# Data Protection and Privacy Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out how Paisa Setu Fintech processes digital personal data in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) and the DPDP Rules, 2025, and other applicable privacy laws.

## 2. Principles

1. **Lawful ground:** we process personal data only with valid consent or for a legitimate use allowed by Section 7 of the DPDP Act.
2. **Notice:** we give a clear, itemised notice before or when asking for consent.
3. **Purpose limitation and minimisation:** we collect only the data needed for the stated purpose.
4. **Accuracy:** we keep personal data accurate and complete where it is used for decisions or shared.
5. **Storage limitation:** we erase personal data when the purpose ends or consent is withdrawn, unless the law requires us to keep it.
6. **Security:** we protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards.
7. **Accountability:** we remain responsible for processing done by our vendors on our behalf.

## 3. Data inventory

The privacy contact maintains an inventory of all processing activities, including data categories, purposes, lawful ground, systems, processors, retention periods and transfers outside India. It is reviewed every 6 months and when new processing starts.

## 4. Consent

Consent is free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given through a clear affirmative action. Users can withdraw consent as easily as they gave it. We keep records of notice versions and consent.

## 5. Rights of Data Principals

We support the rights to access information, correction and erasure, grievance redressal and nomination. Requests are logged, identity is verified, and responses are sent within our internal target of 30 days and never later than 90 days for grievances. Every response includes our privacy contact details.

## 6. Children's data

Paisa Setu Fintech does not knowingly process children's personal data unless verifiable parental consent has been obtained. We do not track, behaviourally monitor or target advertising at children.

## 7. Processors and transfers

We share personal data with processors only under a contract that includes security and data protection obligations. Transfers outside India are recorded and checked against any restrictions notified by the Government and sector regulators.

## 8. Privacy contact

Paisa Setu Fintech's privacy contact or Data Protection Officer is published on our website and app.

## 9. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/policies/4f4b369d-619c-47b2-bd0f-4c0cb8.body_md:
# Data Retention and Disposal Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy defines how long Paisa Setu Fintech keeps information and how it is securely disposed of.

## 2. Retention schedule

| Information | Retention | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer personal data | While the account is active, then erased within 90 days unless legally required | DPDP Act s.8(7) |
| Security and access logs | At least 1 year, stored in India | DPDP Rules R.6(e); CERT-In Directions (v) requires 180 days |
| Incident records | 5 years | Internal requirement |
| Employee records | As required by labour and tax laws | Applicable law |
| Financial records | 8 years | Companies Act / Income Tax Act |
| Backups | 35 days rolling | Internal requirement |

Owners of each information type may set shorter periods where the purpose ends sooner.

## 3. Erasure

1. Personal data is erased when the purpose is complete, consent is withdrawn, or the retention period ends, unless the law requires us to keep it.
2. Where the DPDP Rules require, users are informed at least 48 hours before erasure.
3. Processors are instructed to erase data in the same way, and confirm erasure.

## 4. Secure disposal

1. Digital media is securely wiped or cryptographically erased before re-use or disposal.
2. Devices that cannot be wiped are physically destroyed by an approved vendor, who provides a certificate.
3. Paper records containing confidential or personal data are shredded.

## 5. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

# Acceptable Use Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma
**Applies to:** All employees and contractors using Paisa Setu Fintech devices, accounts, networks or data.

## 1. Purpose

This policy explains how you may and may not use Paisa Setu Fintech systems and information.

## 2. General rules

1. Use company systems mainly for business purposes. Limited personal use is allowed if it does not affect work or security.
2. Use only company-approved tools to store or share company and customer data.
3. Never share your passwords or MFA codes. Use the company password manager.
4. Lock your screen when you step away. Devices lock automatically after 5 minutes of inactivity.
5. Keep devices updated and do not disable encryption, endpoint protection or MDM.
6. Do not install unlicensed or unapproved software.

## 3. Personal data and confidential information

1. Access personal data only when your role needs it.
2. Do not copy customer or employee personal data to personal devices, personal email or personal cloud storage.
3. Do not use real personal data for testing unless it is masked.
4. Do not paste confidential or personal data into public AI tools or websites unless the tool is approved.

## 4. Remote working

1. Work only on company-managed devices.
2. Avoid untrusted public Wi-Fi; use a mobile hotspot or company VPN where required.
3. Keep screens out of view of others and do not print confidential information at home.

## 5. Prohibited use

You must not use company systems to break the law, harass others, access content unrelated to work that creates security risk, attempt to bypass security controls, or access data you are not authorised to see.

## 6. Monitoring

Paisa Setu Fintech monitors its systems for security purposes, in line with applicable law and our employee privacy notice.

## 7. Acknowledgment

All staff acknowledge this policy when they join and once a year.

/help/dashboard.title: Dashboard
/help/dashboard.summary: Your daily starting point - readiness per framework, deadlines, open incidents, controls that need attention, your own work, and one-click incident reporting.
/help/dashboard.body_md:
The dashboard answers three questions: how compliant are we, what is urgent, and what do I need to do?

## Readiness

One card per framework you've turned on, showing the readiness percentage: met requirements out of applicable ones. Click a framework to see its requirements and which controls hold each one back. How the number is calculated is explained in [Key concepts](/docs/concepts#how-readiness-is-calculated).

## Deadlines

Legal and operational deadlines, soonest first, with overdue items highlighted:

- **CERT-In reports**: 6 hours from when a reportable incident was detected;
- **Data Protection Board reports**: the detailed report 72 hours after a personal data breach was detected;
- **Notifying affected people** about a personal data breach;
- **Rights requests** (DPR numbers) approaching their due date;
- **Tasks** with due dates.

## Reporting an incident

**Report incident** (top right) lets anyone except auditors report a security incident or possible data breach in under a minute. Admins are alerted straight away, and you'll get every update about it by email, in one thread. See [Incidents and breaches](/docs/incidents#reporting-an-incident).

## Open incidents

Shown at the top of the dashboard whenever an incident is not closed yet: up to six, most severe first, with when each was noticed and its status. Open one to see its timeline or post an update.

## Controls that need attention

Up to eight controls that are **Failing check** or **Needs evidence**, failing ones first. Open one to see why: the failing check's details or the missing evidence.

## Controls summary

A bar showing how many controls are passing, failing, need evidence, are in progress, not started or not applicable. Use the filters on the **Controls** page to list the controls in any of these states.

## Your work

- **My tasks**: your open tasks, soonest due first.
- **Policies to read and acknowledge**: approved policies you haven't acknowledged in their current version.
- **Vendor reviews due**: vendors whose next review date falls in the next 30 days.

## Recent activity

The latest entries from the audit log: who changed what and when.

/help/tasks.title: Tasks
/help/tasks.summary: The single to-do list for compliance work, including the tasks the platform creates for you.
/help/tasks.body_md:
**Tasks** is where compliance work gets done. You can create tasks yourself, but most are created by the platform when something needs attention.

## Where tasks come from

| Created when | Title starts with | Closes itself? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An integration check fails | Fix: | Yes, when the check passes again |
| An implemented control has no current evidence | Add evidence: | No; mark it done once evidence is added |
| A control's evidence expires within 14 days | Renew evidence: | No; mark it done once fresh evidence is added |
| A policy's yearly review is due | Annual review: | No; close it after re-approving |
| A vendor's review date is due | Review vendor: | No |
| A quarter starts and no access review is running | Start the quarterly access review | No |
| An access review decides to remove an account | Remove (person) from (system) | Yes, when the next sync shows the account gone |
| You create one | (your title) | No |

Tasks linked to a control appear on the control's page too.

## Working with tasks

Each task has a title, description, assignee, due date, priority (low, medium or high) and status (open, in progress or done). The list has three views: **Open**, **Assigned to me** and **Done**.

The platform never creates a duplicate: while a task of the same kind is still open for a control, vendor or policy, no second one is added.

The assignee is emailed when a task is assigned to them, the day before it is due and when it becomes overdue. Overdue tasks also show on the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard).

## Jira

If you connect Jira, tasks at or above a chosen priority are created as Jira issues automatically, and closing the issue in Jira closes the task here. See [Jira](/docs/jira).

/help/frameworks.title: Frameworks
/help/frameworks.summary: The 18 frameworks available, including Indian financial regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA), how to turn them on, conditional requirements, and how to read a framework's status.
/help/frameworks.body_md:
A framework is a law, regulation or standard you need to comply with. Turning one on adds its requirements to your readiness scores and adds any controls it needs that you don't already have.

## Available frameworks

| Framework | Region | Requirements | Who needs it |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| DPDP Act 2023 + DPDP Rules 2025 | India | 49 | Every company processing digital personal data in India, or offering goods and services to people in India |
| CERT-In Directions (April 2022) | India | 7 | Service providers, intermediaries, data centres, body corporates: almost every Indian company with IT systems |
| RBI Cybersecurity, Technology Risk, Resilience and Assurance Directions (2026) | India: financial | 40 | Commercial, small finance, payments and urban co-operative banks, NBFCs (tiered by layer), credit information companies, all-India financial institutions |
| RBI Digital Payment Security Controls Directions (2026) | India: financial | 23 | Banks and credit-card issuing NBFCs offering digital payment products |
| RBI Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security for Non-bank PSOs (2024) | India: financial | 26 | Payment aggregators, wallet (PPI) issuers, card and ATM networks, BBPOUs, TReDS, money transfer operators |
| RBI Payment Aggregators Directions (2025) | India: financial | 25 | Payment aggregators (online, physical and cross-border); payment gateways are recommended to follow the technology baseline |
| RBI Digital Lending Directions (2025) | India: financial | 17 | Banks and NBFCs lending digitally, and their lending service providers and lending apps |
| RBI Outsourcing of IT Services Directions (2023) | India: financial | 15 | Banks, larger NBFCs and other RBI entities that outsource IT; SaaS and fintech vendors serving them through contracts |
| SEBI CSCRF (2024) | India: financial | 24 | Stock brokers, depository participants, AMCs, KRAs, RTAs, portfolio managers, AIFs, market infrastructure |
| IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines (2026) | India: financial | 19 | Insurers and insurance intermediaries (brokers, corporate agents, web aggregators, TPAs) |
| IFSCA Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Guidelines (2025) | India: financial | 12 | Entities licensed or registered by IFSCA in GIFT City |
| ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | Global | 123 | Anyone selling to enterprises; the most widely recognised security certification |
| SOC 2 | Global | 61 | Companies selling to US customers; an attestation report from a CPA firm |
| NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 | Global | 106 | A common language for security programmes; US customers often ask for it |
| PCI DSS v4.0.1 | Global | 63 | Anyone who stores, processes or transmits payment card data |
| ISO/IEC 42001:2023 | Global | 65 | Companies that build, provide or use AI systems |
| EU GDPR | Other regions | 43 | Companies offering services to, or monitoring, people in the EU |
| HIPAA Security and Breach Notification Rules | Other regions | 53 | Companies handling US health data for healthcare customers |

Requirement counts include conditional requirements that may not apply to you.

> **Content status.** Framework guidance is written in-house in plain language and marked "Content in review". Before relying on it for a certification, have it checked by a specialist (a lawyer for laws, a lead auditor for standards). For ISO, AICPA (SOC 2) and PCI SSC content the official text isn't reproduced; buy the standard for the full wording.

## Turning a framework on or off

Open **Frameworks**. Frameworks are grouped as India, India: financial regulators, Global standards and Other regions.

- **Turn on** adds the framework. The platform creates any controls it needs that you don't have and tells you how many were added. Existing controls, evidence and owners are reused.
- **Turn off** removes the framework from your scores. Controls and evidence stay, because other frameworks may use them.

Onboarding suggests a starting set by sector. For example, B2B SaaS gets DPDP, CERT-In, ISO 27001 and SOC 2; NBFC / lending gets DPDP, CERT-In, the RBI Cybersecurity Directions, Digital Lending and IT Outsourcing; Fintech / payments gets the PSO and Payment Aggregator Directions and PCI DSS.

## Conditional requirements and profile questions

Some requirements only apply in certain situations. They switch on when you answer the matching **profile question** in **Settings → Organisation → What applies to you** (questions are grouped by framework, and only shown for frameworks you use):

| Framework | Question | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DPDP | Processes personal data of children or persons with disability | Verifiable parental consent, no tracking or targeted ads for children |
| DPDP | Notified as a Significant Data Fiduciary | DPO in India, independent data audits, DPIAs |
| DPDP | Accepts consent through a registered Consent Manager | Consent Manager integration |
| CERT-In | Provides data centre, VPS, cloud or VPN services | Subscriber records kept for 5 years |
| CERT-In | Virtual asset service provider | KYC and transaction records kept for 5 years |
| SOC 2 | Report includes Processing Integrity | The five PI criteria |
| SOC 2 | Report includes Privacy | The 18 Privacy criteria |
| GDPR | Serves people in the EU without an EU office | Article 27 EU representative |
| PCI DSS | Accepts card payments in person | Payment terminal protection (9.5) |
| PCI DSS | Is a PCI DSS service provider | Customer support for compliance (12.9) |
| HIPAA | Operates a healthcare clearinghouse | Isolating clearinghouse functions |
| RBI Cybersecurity 2026 | Base Layer NBFC below the asset threshold, or a CIC | Only the baseline requirements apply (Chapter III) |
| RBI Cybersecurity 2026 | Base Layer NBFC at or above the threshold | The Chapter IV requirements instead of the full set |
| RBI DPSC 2026 | Offers internet banking / a mobile app / card payments | The channel-specific controls |
| RBI PSO | Card or ATM network / PPI issuer | Card and terminal controls / prepaid instrument controls |
| RBI Payment Aggregators | In-person (PA-P) / cross-border (PA-CB) | Terminal security / cross-border controls |
| IRDAI | Intermediary rather than insurer | The intermediary's audit submission instead of the insurer's |

Requirements that don't apply show as **Not applicable to you** and are excluded from readiness.

## Indian financial regulators

On 31 July 2026 the RBI repealed its 2023 IT Governance Master Direction and the 2016 Cyber Security Framework, and issued Cybersecurity Directions and Digital Payment Security Controls Directions for each type of regulated entity, in force immediately. If you had the old **RBI IT Governance (2023)** framework turned on, the platform moved you to the 2026 Directions automatically. Your controls and evidence carry over because controls are shared; any new controls are added and the change is recorded in the audit log.

Which ones apply to you:

- **Bank or NBFC:** RBI Cybersecurity Directions 2026; add Digital Payment Security Controls if you offer digital payments, Digital Lending if you lend through apps or partners, and IT Outsourcing if you outsource IT. NBFCs: answer the layer questions so only your tier's requirements count.
- **Payment company (PA, wallet, card network):** the non-bank PSO Directions, plus the Payment Aggregators Directions if you're a PA, and PCI DSS.
- **SaaS or fintech vendor to banks and NBFCs:** RBI IT Outsourcing (what your customers must put in your contract), plus ISO 27001 or SOC 2.
- **Stockbroker, AMC, depository participant:** SEBI CSCRF. **Insurer or intermediary:** IRDAI. **GIFT City entity:** IFSCA.

Financial regulators also have their own incident reporting deadlines, usually 6 hours; see [Incidents and breaches](/docs/incidents#financial-regulator-clocks).

These frameworks are marked "Content in review": the 2026 Directions are new and differ slightly between entity types, so check your own entity's Direction on the RBI website.

## Reading a framework

Open a framework to see every requirement grouped by section, with:

- its **status**: Met, Partly met, Not met or Not applicable;
- the **guidance** in plain language;
- the **controls** mapped to it, each with its health, so you can see exactly which control is holding a requirement back.

Use the search box and status filter to find gaps quickly. Click a control to work on it.

## Exports for auditors

From the [Audit workspace](/docs/audit-workspace) you can download, for any framework:

- the **requirements matrix** as Excel; for ISO 27001 this is your **Statement of Applicability**;
- the **evidence pack**: a zip of all current approved evidence with a verification manifest.

/help/controls.title: Controls
/help/controls.summary: Working with controls - statuses, owners, bulk assignment, editing, custom controls, not applicable, and automation.
/help/controls.body_md:
Controls are the heart of the platform: each one is a thing your company does, mapped to every framework requirement it satisfies. See [Key concepts](/docs/concepts#controls) for the basics.

## The controls list

**Controls** lists every control in your organisation with its frameworks, owner, evidence count and health.

Filter by:

- **status** (health): Passing, Failing check, Needs evidence, In progress, Not started, Not applicable;
- **framework**: only controls mapped to that framework;
- **category**: Governance, Access control, Operations, Privacy and so on;
- **owner**: Owned by me, No owner, or anyone;
- **search**: code or title.

A control with uploads waiting for review shows "*n* awaiting review" under its health.

### Assigning owners

Every control should have an owner: the person who makes sure it works and keeps its evidence current. Owners receive reminders and the tasks created for their controls.

- **One control:** pick a person in the **Owner** column; the change saves immediately.
- **Many controls:** tick the checkboxes (or the header box for every control shown), choose a person in the bar that appears and click **Assign**. The same bar can remove owners or set a status in bulk.

New owners get an email listing what they were given. Auditors can't own controls.

## The control page

Open any control to see:

| Panel | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| What the evidence must show | The two or three points evidence must prove, with a tick for each point covered by approved evidence |
| Evidence | Everything attached, with who added and approved it, automatic check results and the AI verdict |
| Automated checks | Results of integration checks mapped to this control, with the last run time |
| Framework requirements | Every requirement this control helps meet, by framework, with guidance |
| Implementation notes | Your description of how the control works here (auditors read this) |
| Details | Status, owner, next review date and the not-applicable reason |
| Collect automatically | Integrations that can provide evidence for this control, and whether they're connected |
| Tasks | Open and completed tasks for the control |

### Setting the status

- **Not started** and **In progress** are for your own tracking.
- **Implemented** means the control is in place. It turns **Passing** once it has current approved evidence and no failing checks.
- **Not applicable** needs a written justification first, because auditors will ask why. N/A controls are excluded from readiness.

### Editing a control

**Edit** changes the title, description, owner, category, review frequency and **what the evidence must show**. Describe controls the way they work in your company; auditors test against your description. The control code and its framework mappings never change, so your scores stay correct.

To go back to the standard evidence criteria, clear the criteria box and save.

### Review frequency

The frequency sets how long new evidence stays valid:

| Frequency | Evidence valid for |
| --- | --- |
| Continuous | 30 days (automated checks refresh it every sync) |
| Monthly | 31 days |
| Quarterly | 92 days |
| Every 6 months | 183 days |
| Yearly | 366 days |
| Once | No expiry |

Fourteen days before the last evidence expires, the platform creates a **Renew evidence** task for the owner. If an implemented control has no evidence at all, it creates an **Add evidence** task.

## Custom controls

**Add custom control** creates a control that isn't in the library, for example for an internal policy or a customer contract requirement. Give it a code (capital letters, digits and dashes, such as CUST-01), title, description, category and frequency. Custom controls work like any other but aren't mapped to framework requirements.

## Automation

A control whose evidence comes from an integration check is the most reliable kind: no one picks or edits the evidence, and it's re-checked every 6 hours. The **Collect automatically** panel shows which integrations could do this for each control. When a check fails:

1. the control's health becomes **Failing check**;
2. a **Fix:** task is created with the details and assigned to the control owner;
3. an alert goes out on your configured channels;
4. when the check passes again, the task closes and the control recovers by itself.

/help/evidence-review.title: Evidence review
/help/evidence-review.summary: How second-person review works, who can approve, how to review well, and the optional AI evidence check.
/help/evidence-review.body_md:
No software can guarantee a document is true. What auditors expect is that **someone other than the person who uploaded evidence has checked it**. The platform enforces this, and gives the reviewer automatic checks and an optional AI opinion to work with.

## How second-person review works

1. Someone uploads a file, link or note. It's marked **Awaiting review** and doesn't count yet.
2. The control's owner (or, if they uploaded it, the admins) get an email, and the item appears in **Evidence review**. The menu shows a count of items waiting for you.
3. A reviewer opens it, checks it against **What the evidence must show**, and either **approves** it or **sends it back** with a reason.
4. Approved evidence counts towards the control. Sent-back evidence never counts, and the uploader is emailed the reason.

Automated and platform-generated evidence is approved automatically.

## Who can review

- **Admins and owners** can review any evidence.
- A **control's owner** can review evidence on their controls, even as a member.
- **Nobody can approve their own upload** when someone else could. The only exception is a one-person organisation, where the uploader may approve their own evidence. That approval is labelled **Self-approved** everywhere, including the evidence pack, so the auditor knows.
- **Auditors can't review.** Their acceptance happens in the [Audit workspace](/docs/audit-workspace).

## The review queue

**Evidence review** has two tabs:

- **Waiting**: evidence awaiting review. Filter to **For me to review**, **With warnings** or **Everything waiting**. Each item shows the control, its acceptance criteria, what the uploader says it shows, the automatic check results and the AI verdict, with **Approve** and **Send back** buttons.
- **Recently reviewed**: the last 20 decisions, with who made them and when.

## How to review well

For each item, ask:

1. **Is it for this control?** A password policy isn't proof of MFA.
2. **Does it show each point** the uploader ticked, and do those points match **What the evidence must show**?
3. **Is it ours and current?** Our company or tenant name, dated in this review period.
4. **Is it complete?** A filled-in, signed document, not a template or draft.
5. **What do the warnings say?** A reused file or an old date usually means it should be sent back.

When you send something back, say exactly what's needed: "Upload this quarter's scan with the remediation status" is better than "wrong file".

## AI evidence check

When turned on, Claude (Anthropic's AI model) reads each new piece of evidence (the image, the PDF, or the text of Word, Excel and other documents) and compares it with the control's criteria. It reports:

- a verdict: **Looks right**, **Needs attention** or **Doesn't fit this control**;
- a short summary;
- for each criterion: shown, not shown or unclear, with a reason;
- specific issues, such as "placeholders are still present" or "dated before the review period";
- the organisation named in the document. If that isn't your company, the verdict becomes "Doesn't fit this control".

The verdict is **advice for the reviewer, never a decision**: it doesn't approve or reject anything. Documents can contain text written to fool an AI; the check treats file contents strictly as data, and any attempt to influence it counts against the evidence.

### Turning it on

Only the **owner** can turn it on, in **Settings → Security → Evidence checks**, and only after turning on the AI assistant. Because this sends uploaded evidence files to Anthropic's API, the owner must confirm that explicitly. Turning off the AI assistant turns evidence checks off too. The server also needs an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting)).

Evidence checks run in the background, usually within a minute, and don't count towards the assistant's daily limit. If a check can't run, the item says so and the reviewer simply reviews it without one.

## Turning review off

Admins can turn second-person review off in **Settings → Security → Evidence checks**; new uploads then count immediately. We don't recommend it: auditors look for this separation of duties, and many standards (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS) expect it.

/policies/8a59ec70-62e1-49b4-8af7-361468.body_md:
# Incident Response Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy defines how Paisa Setu Fintech detects, responds to, reports and learns from security incidents and personal data breaches.

## 2. Reporting by staff

Anyone who suspects a security incident, phishing attempt, lost device or data exposure must report it immediately to the security team through the incident channel. Do not investigate on your own or delete evidence.

## 3. Severity levels

| Level | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SEV-1 | Confirmed breach of personal or customer data, or major outage | Database exposed publicly |
| SEV-2 | Likely compromise with limited impact | Compromised employee account |
| SEV-3 | Suspicious event needing investigation | Phishing email reported |

## 4. Response process

1. **Triage:** decide whether the event is an incident and assign severity and an incident lead.
2. **Contain:** limit the impact (revoke credentials, isolate systems).
3. **Preserve evidence:** keep logs and system images with a record of who handled them.
4. **Eradicate and recover:** remove the cause and restore services safely.
5. **Communicate:** keep leadership, affected customers and regulators informed as required.
6. **Review:** hold a post-incident review for SEV-1 and SEV-2 incidents and track actions.

## 5. Regulatory reporting

| Authority | Trigger | Deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CERT-In | Incident types listed in Annexure I of the CERT-In Directions | Within 6 hours of noticing |
| Data Protection Board | Any personal data breach | Without delay; detailed report within 72 hours |
| Affected Data Principals | Any personal data breach affecting them | Without delay |
| Sector regulator (if applicable) | As per sector rules (for example RBI, SEBI) | As per sector rules |

The incident lead records the time the incident was noticed. The platform tracks each deadline from that time. The DPO or privacy contact approves notices to Data Principals and the Board.

## 6. Testing

The incident response plan is tested at least once a year through a tabletop exercise.

## 7. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually and after every SEV-1 incident.

/policies/3777aa9f-fd84-4842-8060-e3c5cd.body_md:
# Information Security Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma
**Applies to:** All employees, contractors and third parties with access to Paisa Setu Fintech information or systems.

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out how Paisa Setu Fintech protects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the information it holds, including personal data of customers and employees. It is the top-level policy of our information security programme. Topic-specific policies support it.

## 2. Objectives

Paisa Setu Fintech commits to:

1. Protect customer and company information from unauthorised access, change or loss.
2. Meet legal, regulatory and contractual requirements, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its Rules, the CERT-In Directions of April 2022, and customer contracts.
3. Identify and treat information security risks on a regular basis.
4. Report and respond to security incidents quickly, including reporting to CERT-In within 6 hours and to the Data Protection Board as required.
5. Continually improve the information security programme.

Leadership sets measurable security objectives each year and reviews progress at least annually.

## 3. Roles and responsibilities

- **Leadership** approves this policy, provides resources and reviews the programme at least once a year.
- **Security lead** runs the programme, maintains policies, coordinates risk assessments and audits, and reports to leadership.
- **Privacy contact / Data Protection Officer** owns DPDP obligations, data principal requests and breach notifications.
- **Control owners** operate the controls assigned to them and keep evidence current.
- **All staff** follow security policies, complete training, and report suspected incidents immediately.

## 4. Policy framework

This policy is supported by topic-specific policies, including Acceptable Use, Access Control, Incident Response, Data Protection and Privacy, Data Retention, Vendor Management, and Business Continuity. All policies are reviewed at least annually and after significant change.

## 5. Compliance and exceptions

Compliance with security policies is checked through internal audits and automated monitoring. Exceptions must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, approved by the security lead and recorded with an expiry date. Violations may lead to disciplinary action.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least every 12 months by the security lead and approved by leadership.

/policies/771e5112-a8ac-4fa6-ac71-f36f1d.title: Vendor Management Policy
/policies/771e5112-a8ac-4fa6-ac71-f36f1d.body_md:
# Vendor Management Policy

**Company:** Paisa Setu Fintech
**Owner:** Priya Sharma

## 1. Purpose

This policy makes sure vendors who access Paisa Setu Fintech systems or data meet our security and data protection requirements.

## 2. Vendor inventory and tiers

All vendors are recorded in the vendor inventory with an owner and a risk tier:

| Tier | Criteria | Review frequency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | Processes customer personal data or is essential to service delivery | Annually |
| High | Accesses internal confidential data or production systems | Annually |
| Medium | Limited access to internal data | Every 2 years |
| Low | No access to data or systems | At onboarding only |

## 3. Onboarding

Before a Critical or High vendor is engaged:

1. The vendor completes a security questionnaire or provides an independent report (ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report).
2. The security lead reviews the results and records the decision.
3. A contract is signed with security requirements, breach notification duties, audit rights and, where personal data is shared, a Data Processing Agreement covering DPDP obligations.

## 4. Ongoing monitoring

Vendors are reassessed according to their tier. Significant changes, incidents or expiring certifications trigger a new review.

## 5. Offboarding

When a relationship ends, access is revoked and the vendor confirms return or erasure of Paisa Setu Fintech data.

## 6. Review

This policy is reviewed at least annually.

/help/policies.title: Policies
/help/policies.summary: Bring in or write policies, approve them, version them, collect staff acknowledgments and keep them reviewed.
/help/policies.body_md:
Policies are the written rules auditors read first. The platform manages their whole life: drafting, approval, staff acknowledgment, yearly review and evidence.

## Adding a policy

**Policies → New policy** gives four ways in:

| Option | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| **Upload a document** | You already have policies in Word (.docx), PDF, Markdown, text or HTML. Headings, lists, bold and tables are converted so you can edit them here. PDFs keep text only, so check the formatting. Scanned PDFs have no text; paste instead. Old .doc files must be saved as .docx first. |
| **Paste from Google Docs or Word** | Copy the whole document (Ctrl/Cmd+A, then Ctrl/Cmd+C) and paste into the editor. Formatting is kept; scripts and styles are stripped. |
| **Write from scratch** | Use the editor's toolbar: headings, bold, italic, links, lists, quotes, dividers and tables. No formatting codes needed. |
| **Start from a template** | Eight templates written for Indian companies, covering DPDP and CERT-In: information security, access control, acceptable use, data protection, data retention, incident response, business continuity and vendor management. |

When saving, choose the **owner** (who keeps it up to date) and the **controls it supports**. Imported files are converted (Word and PDF on the server, other formats in your browser) and the file itself is never stored; only the text you save is kept.

The editor has a **Markdown** view for people who prefer it, and an **Import file** button to replace the content from a document at any time.

## Approval and versions

- A new policy starts as a **Draft**.
- An admin clicks **Approve version 1**. The policy becomes **Approved**, gets a review date (usually one year ahead), and is attached as evidence to every control it supports.
- Editing an approved policy creates a new **draft version** (version 2 and so on). The approved version stays in force as evidence until the new one is approved.

## Staff acknowledgment

When a policy is approved, everyone in the organisation is asked to read and acknowledge it (it appears on their dashboard under **Policies to read and acknowledge**). Each new version needs a fresh acknowledgment. The policies list shows how many people have acknowledged the current version, for example "18 of 22".

## Yearly review

When a policy's review date approaches, an **Annual review** task is created for its owner. Review it, make any changes and approve again.

## Other actions

- **Download (.md)** saves the policy text.
- **Delete** (admins only) removes the policy and its acknowledgments.
- The [AI assistant](/docs/ai-assistant), if your owner has turned it on, can draft a policy from your existing policies and controls.

/help/audit-workspace.title: Audit workspace
/help/audit-workspace.summary: Working with your auditor - auditor accounts, evidence requests, the requirements matrix and Statement of Applicability, evidence packs and sampling.
/help/audit-workspace.body_md:
The **Audit workspace** is where your team and your auditor work together, instead of email threads and shared folders. Every request, comment, test and download is in the audit log.

## Give your auditor an account

In **Settings → Team**, invite the auditor with the **Auditor** role and the number of days they need (for example 60 for an audit season). They can read everything but change nothing, and their access ends automatically on that date. See [Roles and permissions](/docs/roles-and-permissions#auditor).

## Evidence requests

Auditors (and admins) raise **requests** for specific evidence:

1. **New request**: a title, description, optionally the framework requirement or control it relates to, an assignee on your team and a due date. The assignee is emailed.
2. Your team **submits** evidence: select existing evidence items, add a note and submit. Comments on the request keep the conversation in one place.
3. The auditor **accepts** the evidence or **rejects** it with a comment, and your team responds.

Filter requests by status: Open, Evidence submitted, Accepted.

## Exports

At the top of the workspace, choose a framework and download:

- the **requirements matrix** (Excel): every requirement with whether it applies (and why not, if it doesn't), its status, the controls that implement it with their implementation notes, the number of current evidence items and the control owners. For ISO 27001 this serves as your **Statement of Applicability**;
- the **evidence pack** (zip).

### Evidence pack

The evidence pack contains every current, **approved** evidence item for the framework's controls, in a folder per control:

- uploaded files, decrypted, exactly as uploaded;
- automated results, policies and notes as JSON files;
- `manifest.json` listing every file with its SHA-256 hash, who added it, who approved it and when, whether it was self-approved, automatic check warnings, the AI verdict, and for uploaded files the fingerprint taken at upload with `unchanged_since_upload`;
- `README.txt` explaining how to verify the files, and how many items were still awaiting review (those aren't included).

The manifest's own hash is written to the tamper-evident audit log when the pack is downloaded, so the pack can be verified later.

## Evidence sampling

Auditors don't check every item; they test a random **sample** in depth. **Evidence sampling** does this properly:

1. **New sample**: name it, choose a framework (or all), the period the evidence was collected in, the sample size (1 to 200) and the method:
   - **At least one per control**: one random item from each control, then random items up to the size;
   - **Simple random**: random items from the whole population.
2. The platform draws the sample from **approved** evidence only and saves the **random seed**. With the same seed and population, anyone can re-perform the selection, which auditors need to show the sample wasn't hand-picked.
3. For each item, open the file or link and record **Pass** or **Exception** (an exception needs a description). The tester and time are recorded.
4. The sample flags any item whose file **changed after it was sampled**, or was deleted.
5. **Export to Excel** gives the full working paper: population, size, seed, each item with uploader, approver, warnings, AI verdict, result, notes, tester and time.

Both auditors and admins can draw samples and record results; admins can use this for internal audits.

/help/training.title: Security training
/help/training.summary: Built-in and company courses, required training by department, due dates for new joiners, certificates, team progress and imports.
/help/training.body_md:
Security and privacy awareness training is required by almost every framework (HR-03). The platform runs the whole programme: courses, who must take what, reminders, certificates and the report your auditor asks for.

## The four tabs

| Tab | Who sees it | What it's for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| My learning | Everyone | Your assigned courses, due dates and certificates; optional courses |
| Team progress | Admins and auditors | Who has completed what, by department and person; exports and imports |
| Courses and assignments | Admins | Choose which courses are required and for whom; create company courses |
| Phishing simulations | Admins | See [Phishing simulations](/docs/phishing-simulations) |

## Built-in courses

| Course | Category | Minutes |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Security essentials | Foundations | 12 |
| Spotting phishing and social engineering (with practice exercises) | Foundations | 10 |
| Passwords, MFA and keeping your accounts safe | Foundations | 8 |
| UPI, KYC and 'digital arrest' scams (with practice exercises) | Foundations | 10 |
| Spotting and reporting security incidents | Foundations | 7 |
| Using AI tools safely at work | Foundations | 8 |
| Working securely from home and on the move | Foundations | 7 |
| India's DPDP Act for everyone at work | Privacy | 15 |
| Classifying and sharing data safely | Privacy | 8 |
| Secure development for engineers | Role-based | 15 |
| Payment fraud and business email compromise (with practice exercises) | Role-based: finance and procurement | 10 |
| Handling personal data in customer support | Role-based: support and operations | 10 |

Each course has a short lesson and a five-question quiz with a pass mark (usually 80%). Answers are shuffled, the correct answers stay on the server, and after submitting you see an explanation for each question. Some courses have **practice exercises**: realistic messages to judge as phishing or legitimate, which don't count towards the score.

## Who must take what

In **Courses and assignments**, each course is either **optional** or **required**. For a required course you set:

- **who**: everyone, or only certain departments from the HR roster;
- **days to complete** (default 30);
- **renew every** (default 12 months).

Security essentials, the phishing course and DPDP basics are required for everyone by default. If your roster has Engineering, Finance or Support departments, the matching role-based courses are required for them automatically.

### Due dates

- **New joiners** get the full number of days from their **joining date**.
- **Existing staff** get the full number of days from the date the course became required.
- Someone who **clicks a phishing simulation** can be enrolled in the phishing course with 14 days to complete it, even if they passed it before.

Completions expire after the renewal period, and the person is asked to take the course again.

## Certificates

Passing a course produces a certificate with the person's name, course, score, completion date, valid-until date and a certificate ID. Open it from the course or the course card, then **Print or save as PDF**.

## Team progress

- **Everyone fully trained**: the percentage of all staff, including people in the HR roster who don't have an account yet. Auditors expect every employee to be trained.
- **People with an account fully trained**.
- **In the HR roster without an account**, with **Invite them** to email everyone missing an invitation.
- Completion **by department**, with overdue counts. Click a department to filter.
- A table of every person and their status for each required course: Completed, To do, Overdue, Renewal due or Not passed.

**Export CSV** gives the auditor-ready report: name, email, department, course, status, due date, last completion and score.

## Importing from another learning platform

If people completed training elsewhere, **Import from another LMS** accepts a CSV with columns `email`, `course` (the course name or ID) and `completed_at`, plus `score` if you have it. Imported completions count like any other.

## Company courses

**Create a course** to teach your own policies, tools or client requirements. Add a title and summary, write the content (paste from Google Docs or Word, or import a document), optionally link a video (https), and build a quiz: questions with 2 to 6 options and an explanation. Save as a draft, then **Publish** and assign it like any other course.

## Reminders and the HR-03 check

Each person with overdue or expired required training receives a weekly reminder. Every day the platform checks whether at least 90% of staff are fully trained, and records the result as an automated check on **HR-03**, so the control's health reflects reality.
