/help/ai-assistant.title: AI assistant
/help/ai-assistant.summary: Draft policies, plan remediation from gaps and answer customer security questionnaires from your own documents - and what data the AI sees.
/help/ai-assistant.body_md:
The AI assistant uses Claude, Anthropic's AI model, to take the first pass at writing work. It works from your own policies and controls and cites them, and people review everything before it's used.

## Turning it on

The assistant is **off by default**. The **owner** turns it on in **Settings → Security → AI assistant**, after confirming that policy and control text may be sent to the AI provider. The server needs an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (see [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting)). Each organisation can run up to 40 assistant jobs a day.

## What it can do

### Draft a policy

Give a topic (for example "Bring your own device"), optional notes and the controls it must cover. The assistant drafts a policy in your tone, consistent with your existing policies, with sections for purpose, scope, roles, numbered policy statements, exceptions and review. Unknown facts are left as `[TODO: …]` placeholders and listed as open questions. **Save as policy** creates a draft for normal [approval](/docs/policies#approval-and-versions).

### Gap analysis and remediation plan

Pick a framework. The assistant reviews unmet requirements and your controls' states and suggests a prioritised plan: what to do first and why.

### Answer a customer's security questionnaire

Upload the customer's questionnaire (Excel or CSV with a question column), or paste questions. The assistant answers each one **from your own policies and controls**, citing the sources it used, and marks low-confidence answers where your documents don't support an answer. Edit the answers, then **export to Excel** to send back. This can turn days of work into an hour of review.

## What is sent to the AI

| Sent | Never sent |
| --- | --- |
| Your policy text, control descriptions and implementation notes | People data (roster, accounts) |
| Framework requirements and guidance | Consent records and rights requests |
| The topic, notes or questions you enter | Credentials and API keys |
| | Evidence files, unless the owner separately turns on [AI evidence checks](/docs/evidence-review#ai-evidence-check) |

## How it stays safe

- Everything retrieved from your workspace is passed as data, with an instruction never to follow instructions inside it.
- Answers must come back in a fixed format; anything else is rejected. Citations to documents that weren't sent are removed.
- Nothing is acted on automatically. Drafts become policies only when you save them, and answers go to customers only when you export them.

/help/integrations.title: Integrations
/help/integrations.summary: How integrations work, connecting them safely, automation coverage, and the full catalogue of 25 integrations and their checks.
/help/integrations.body_md:
Integrations connect the platform to the tools you already use. They collect evidence and run checks automatically, so controls stay current without anyone uploading screenshots.

## How integrations work

1. You connect a tool with **read-only** credentials. Credentials are encrypted at rest and never shown again.
2. The platform runs the integration's **checks** straight away, then **every 6 hours**.
3. Each check maps to one or more controls:
   - **pass**: an automated evidence item is saved or refreshed on those controls, labelled "Collected automatically";
   - **fail**: the controls show **Failing check**, a **Fix:** task is created for the control owner with the details, and an alert goes to your notification channels;
   - when a failing check passes again, the task closes and the control recovers by itself.
4. Identity, cloud, code and device integrations also import **accounts** (who has access, and whether they're an admin), which power leaver checks and [access reviews](/docs/people-and-access). HR integrations import the **roster**.

Every integration is read-only except Jira, which creates issues when you ask it to.

## Connecting

**Integrations → Connect** on the tool, then fill in the fields. Each field explains where to find the value in that tool, and which read-only role or scope to grant. **Connect and run checks** verifies the credentials and runs the first sync.

On a connected integration:

- **Run checks**: sync now instead of waiting for the next scheduled run;
- **Update credentials**: rotate the key or token;
- **Disconnect**: stop syncing. Existing evidence stays until it expires.

Customer-supplied addresses (your Okta domain, Jira site, Jamf URL and so on) must be HTTPS and, in production, public. The platform refuses internal addresses to protect your network.

## Automation coverage

The **Automation coverage** panel shows, for your controls:

- how many are **fully automated** (an integration check covers them);
- how many are **one-click**: evidence is produced as a by-product of using the platform (policies, training, access reviews, vendor reviews, consent records);
- how many are **manual**: governance, HR paperwork and physical controls that need a document;
- **Connect next**: the integrations that would automate the most controls you have.

## Your own tools: the evidence API

For checks no integration covers (a backup restore test in your CI, a Jenkins job, a custom script), push results to the [evidence API](/docs/api#evidence-api) with an API key. A passing result becomes automated evidence on the controls you name; a failing one fails them.

## Catalogue

Numbers in brackets are the controls each check provides evidence for.

### Identity

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Google Workspace | 2-Step Verification enforced for all active users (ACC-03); all active users enrolled in 2-Step Verification (ACC-03); super admin count within limit (ACC-04); no active accounts unused for 90+ days (ACC-02, ACC-05). Imports users. |
| Microsoft 365 / Entra ID | MFA required for all users through Security defaults or Conditional Access (ACC-03); all members registered for MFA (ACC-03); Global Administrator count within limit (ACC-04). Imports users. |
| Okta | Sign-in policy requires MFA for all apps (ACC-03); all active users enrolled in MFA (ACC-03); admin count within limit (ACC-04); no dormant active accounts (ACC-05, ACC-02). Imports users. |

### Cloud

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Amazon Web Services | Root account MFA (ACC-03, ACC-04); IAM password policy 12+ characters (ACC-08); multi-region CloudTrail logging (LOG-01); S3 account-level public access block (NET-01, ACC-06); EBS encryption by default (CRY-01); RDS encrypted at rest (CRY-01); RDS backups kept 7+ days (OPS-06); GuardDuty enabled (LOG-02); Security Hub with a standard (OPS-04, LOG-02); Inspector scanning (OPS-02); AWS Backup plan with resources (OPS-06); CloudWatch logs kept 180+ days (LOG-01); access keys rotated within 90 days (ACC-08); production in its own account (SDL-04). Imports IAM users. |
| Microsoft Azure | Defender for Cloud Standard tier (OPS-01, LOG-02); storage enforces TLS 1.2 and blocks public blobs (NET-02, ACC-06, CRY-01); activity log exported (LOG-01); subscription Owner count within limit (ACC-04); resources hosted in Indian regions, optional (PRV-13, LOG-01). |
| Google Cloud | Project owner count within limit (ACC-04); no IAM roles for allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers (ACC-06); buckets enforce public access prevention (ACC-06); no user-managed service account keys (ACC-08); data access audit logs on (LOG-01). |

### Source code

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub | Organisation requires 2FA (ACC-03); default branches require pull request review (SDL-02, SDL-05); secret scanning on all repositories (ACC-08, SDL-03); Dependabot alerts on (OPS-02, SDL-03); no critical or high Dependabot alerts past the fix deadline (OPS-02, SDL-03); org admin count within limit (ACC-04, ACC-07). Imports members. |
| GitLab | Group requires 2FA (ACC-03); default branches protected, no direct developer pushes (SDL-02, SDL-05); merge requests need an approval (SDL-02); group owner count within limit (ACC-04, ACC-07). Imports members. |
| Bitbucket Cloud | Main branches require an approval and block direct pushes (SDL-02, SDL-05). |

### Devices

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Microsoft Intune | Devices encrypted (AST-05, CRY-01); devices compliant (AST-05, OPS-04); devices checked in within 30 days (AST-01). |
| Jamf Pro | FileVault on all Macs (AST-05, CRY-01); Macs checked in within 30 days (AST-01); supported macOS version (OPS-02, AST-05). |
| Scalefusion (beta) | Devices encrypted, compliant and checked in within 30 days. |
| Hexnode UEM (beta) | Devices encrypted, compliant and checked in within 30 days. |

### Vulnerability scanning and endpoint security

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Snyk | Code and dependencies are being scanned (SDL-03, OPS-02); no critical or high issues past the fix deadline (OPS-02, SDL-03). |
| Tenable Vulnerability Management | A scan completed in the last 30 days (OPS-02); no critical or high vulnerabilities past the fix deadline (OPS-02). |
| CrowdStrike Falcon | Sensors reported within 7 days (OPS-01, AST-05); no high or critical alerts open over 7 days (OPS-01, LOG-02). |
| SentinelOne | Agents active and reporting within 7 days (OPS-01, AST-05); no unresolved threats (OPS-01, LOG-02). |

Fix deadlines for vulnerabilities are configurable per integration (for example critical within 15 days, high within 30).

### Monitoring, network and IT

| Integration | Checks |
| --- | --- |
| Datadog | Log indexes keep logs for the required period, default 180 days for CERT-In (LOG-01); alert monitors exist and notify someone (LOG-02, OPS-05). |
| Cloudflare | Every site forces HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and strict origin certificates (NET-02). |
| Freshservice | IT asset inventory updated in the last 90 days (AST-01); changes recorded through change management (SDL-05, RISK-04). |

### HR (roster import, beta)

Keka, Darwinbox, greytHR and Zoho People import employees, managers, departments, and joining and exit dates for leaver checks, access reviews and training. Field mappings should be checked against your own data the first time.

### Work tracking

Jira creates and syncs issues for tasks and risks. See [Jira](/docs/jira).

## Demo data

Demo organisations have simulated connections with sample results. They can't be synced; connect your real tools in your own organisation.

/help/people-and-access.title: People, accounts and access reviews
/help/people-and-access.summary: The HR roster, matching people to their accounts, leaver checks, and quarterly access reviews routed to managers.
/help/people-and-access.body_md:
Several controls depend on knowing who works for you and what they can access: joiners and leavers (ACC-02, HR-05), access reviews (ACC-05) and training (HR-03). The platform brings this together from your HR system and your connected tools.

## The HR roster

**People & accounts** holds your roster: everyone who works for you, with email, name, employee ID, department, title, manager's email, status, joining date and exit date.

There are two ways to fill it:

- **Connect your HR system**: Keka, Darwinbox, greytHR or Zoho People (all in beta). The roster refreshes on every sync.
- **Upload a CSV**: export from your HR system or a spreadsheet. Only an email column is required. Column names are recognised flexibly; for example "Official Email", "DOJ", "Reporting Manager Email" and "Last Working Day" all work. Dates can be in common Indian and international formats (31-03-2026, 31/03/2026, 31 Mar 2026, 2026-03-31). A status such as "exited", "relieved", "resigned", "terminated" or "absconded", or an exit date in the past, marks a person as a leaver.

Departments from the roster drive department-based [training](/docs/training) and phishing simulations.

## Accounts

Every identity, cloud and code integration also imports the **accounts** in that system: who has an account, whether it's active, and whether it has admin rights. **People & accounts** shows each person with their accounts across systems, so you can see at a glance who has access to what.

## Leaver check

Every sync, the platform checks whether anyone who has **left** (by status or exit date) still has an **active account** in a connected system, allowing one day's grace after the exit date. If so, the automated check "Leavers have no active accounts" fails on ACC-02 and HR-05, a task is created, and the accounts are listed in a red banner at the top of **People & accounts** so you can remove them.

## Access reviews

An access review confirms that everyone with access to a system should still have it. Most frameworks expect one every quarter for important systems.

### Running a review

1. **Access reviews → Start access review**: give it a title (for example "Q3 2026 access review"), pick the systems (any connected integration with accounts) and optionally a due date (default 14 days) and a default reviewer.
2. The platform takes a snapshot of every active account in those systems and **routes each one to the person's manager** (from the HR roster). Accounts without a known manager go to the default reviewer. **Nobody reviews their own access.**
3. Reviewers get an email and decide for each account: **Keep** or **Remove**. Removing needs a short reason.
4. Each removal creates a task to remove the access. On the next sync the platform checks the account is gone, and closes the task by itself when it is.
5. When every account has a decision, an admin clicks **Complete review**. The signed-off review (CSV) is attached as evidence to **ACC-05 Periodic access reviews**, valid for 92 days.

At the start of each quarter, if no review is running, the platform creates a **Start the quarterly access review** task. Reviews can be exported to CSV at any time.

/help/data-inventory.title: Data inventory
/help/data-inventory.summary: Your record of processing - every activity that uses personal data, its purpose, lawful ground, retention, processors and transfers.
/help/data-inventory.body_md:
The **data inventory** (also called a record of processing activities) lists every way your organisation uses personal data. It's the foundation for DPDP notices, rights requests, breach assessments and the PRV-01 control, and auditors under GDPR and ISO 27701 ask for the same thing.

## What to record for each processing activity

| Field | What to enter | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Processing activity name | A short name | Customer onboarding (KYC) |
| Description | What happens | We verify identity and address before opening an account |
| Systems | Where the data lives | Core app (Postgres), S3 document store, Signzy |
| Data principals | Whose data | Customers, applicants |
| Data categories | What data | Name, phone, PAN, Aadhaar (masked), address, selfie |
| Purposes | Why | Account opening and regulatory KYC |
| Lawful ground | Consent, or a legitimate use under DPDP s.7 | Legitimate use |
| Which legitimate use | Required when the ground is legitimate use | Compliance with law (RBI KYC Master Direction) |
| Retention period | How long, and the trigger | 5 years after account closure |
| Processors | Vendors that process it | Signzy, AWS |
| Stored or accessed outside India | Tick if so, and list the countries | No |
| Includes children's data (under 18) | Triggers the children's data rules | No |
| Owner | Who is responsible | Head of Operations |
| Last reviewed | When it was last checked | 2026-09-30 |

## Building it quickly

1. Start with your main products and internal functions: customer accounts, payments, support, marketing, HR and payroll, recruitment.
2. Use [Data discovery](/docs/data-discovery) to scan your databases and storage. Its findings can be added to the inventory in one click with **Add to data inventory**.
3. Ask each system owner to check their activities.
4. Review the inventory at least yearly, and whenever you launch a feature that uses personal data, then update **Last reviewed**.

## How it's used elsewhere

- **Rights requests**: the inventory tells you where to look for a person's data.
- **Incidents**: it helps you work out whose data, and which categories, were affected.
- **Cross-border transfers**: activities marked as stored outside India feed PRV-13.
- **Evidence**: an export of the inventory is the evidence for PRV-01.

/help/consent-records.title: Consent records
/help/consent-records.summary: Versioned consent notices, a tamper-proof log of every grant and withdrawal from your website and apps, and a feed of withdrawals to act on.
/help/consent-records.body_md:
Under the DPDP Act, consent must be free, specific, informed and unambiguous, and **withdrawing it must be as easy as giving it**. You must also be able to show what a person agreed to, and when. **Consent records** gives you exactly that.

## How it works

1. You write a **consent notice** with purposes, and publish it. Each published change creates a new version.
2. When someone agrees (or withdraws) on your website or app, your system sends a record to the platform's [Consent API](/docs/api#consent-api).
3. The platform keeps an **append-only log**: records can't be edited or deleted, not even by admins. Each record stores the person's ID in your system, the notice and version, the purposes, the source, the language and the time.
4. Your systems poll the **withdrawals feed** and stop processing for withdrawn purposes, including telling your processors.

## The three tabs

### Records

Totals for the last 30 days (consents, withdrawals, people on record, last record), the latest records, and **Look up a person by your user ID** to see their full consent history: what they agreed to, which notice version, when, and any withdrawals. **Export** downloads the log as CSV for auditors or for answering an access request.

You can also record consent given on paper or over a call centre line manually; the source is recorded as such.

### Consent notices

Each notice has:

- a **key** (for example `marketing` or `kyc-onboarding`) that your code refers to;
- a **title** and **notice text** (Markdown): what you collect, why, how to withdraw, and how to complain;
- **purposes**: each with an ID (used in the API), a label, and whether it's **required** for the service;
- **languages** offered. DPDP expects notices in English or any of the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule, as the person chooses.

Edit as a draft, then **Publish** (admins). Published versions never change; publishing an edit creates the next version, and new records default to the latest published version.

### Connect your app

A step-by-step guide with copyable examples:

1. **Create an API key** with the `consent:write` scope (and `consent:read` for the systems that read the withdrawals feed) in **Settings → Security → API keys**.
2. **Send a record when someone agrees or withdraws.**
3. **Act on withdrawals** by polling the feed.

The full request and response formats are in the [API reference](/docs/api#consent-api).

## Automated check

Every day the platform checks that consent is being recorded and that withdrawals are captured, and records the result on **PRV-03** (consent capture) and **PRV-04** (withdrawal).

## Consent Managers

DPDP's registered Consent Managers start from 13 November 2026. Records that arrive through a Consent Manager can already carry its reference (`source: consent_manager`, `consent_manager_ref`). A direct integration will follow once the Board publishes the interface.

/help/data-discovery.title: Data discovery
/help/data-discovery.summary: Scan databases and storage buckets for Indian and other personal data, safely, and turn findings into data inventory entries.
/help/data-discovery.body_md:
You can't protect personal data you don't know you have. **Data discovery** scans your databases and storage for personal data (Aadhaar and PAN numbers, phone numbers, UPI IDs and more) and shows where it is, so you can complete your [data inventory](/docs/data-inventory) and apply the right controls.

## What it detects

Detection combines **column names** (such as `aadhaar_no`, `dob` or `mobile`) with **value patterns** checked on sampled values:

| Category | Detected by |
| --- | --- |
| Aadhaar number | Value pattern (12 digits, not starting 0 or 1) and column names |
| PAN | Value pattern (format AAAPA1234A) and column names |
| GSTIN | Value pattern |
| Payment card number | Value pattern |
| UPI ID | Value pattern with known UPI handles (okaxis, ybl, paytm and others) |
| Phone number | Indian mobile number pattern and column names |
| Email address | Value pattern and column names |
| IFSC code | Value pattern |
| Passport, voter ID, date of birth, address, name, bank account, gender | Column names |
| Health and biometric data | Column names (diagnosis, blood group, fingerprint and similar) |

## What leaves your systems

Scans are **read-only** and **sampled**: up to 200 rows per table across up to 300 tables, or up to 200 objects (256 KB each) in a bucket. Only the **category, counts and masked examples** are stored, never raw values. For example, an Aadhaar number is kept only as `XXXX XXXX 1234`.

## Two ways to scan

### From the platform (direct)

**Add data source**: give it a name and choose PostgreSQL, MySQL or Amazon S3, then enter connection details for a **read-only** user (database host, port, database, username, password; or bucket, prefix, region and an access key). Credentials are encrypted. Click **Scan** to run it.

In production the platform only connects to public addresses. Databases on private networks need the agent.

### Self-hosted scanner agent (private networks)

For databases inside your network, run the scanner agent there. It reads data locally and sends only categories, counts and masked examples. The platform masks examples again whatever the agent sends.

1. Create an API key with the `scanner:write` scope.
2. Create an environment file:

~~~
PRAMAANLY_URL=https://app.yourcompany.com
PRAMAANLY_API_KEY=prm_...
SCAN_NAME=orders-db (prod)
SCAN_KIND=postgres
SCAN_HOST=10.0.3.12
SCAN_PORT=5432
SCAN_DATABASE=orders
SCAN_USERNAME=readonly_scanner
SCAN_PASSWORD=...
~~~

3. Run it with Docker:

~~~
docker run --rm --env-file scan.env pramaanly/backend python -m app.agent
~~~

For S3 use `SCAN_KIND=s3` with `SCAN_BUCKET`, `SCAN_PREFIX`, `SCAN_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Set `SCAN_DRY_RUN=1` to print the report instead of sending it. Schedule it with cron to keep findings current.

## Findings

Findings are grouped by source and table or object, with the categories found, how many sampled values matched, and masked examples. Select findings and **Add to data inventory** to create or update a processing activity with those systems and data categories.

/help/rights-requests.title: Rights requests and the privacy request page
/help/rights-requests.summary: Receive, verify and answer data principal requests on time, including through a public request page with email verification.
/help/rights-requests.body_md:
Under the DPDP Act, people can ask you to give them information about their data, correct or erase it, nominate someone to act for them, withdraw consent, and raise grievances. **Rights requests** tracks each one from receipt to answer, with due dates.

## Request types

| Type | What the person wants |
| --- | --- |
| Access | A summary of their personal data and how it's processed |
| Correction | Inaccurate or incomplete data fixed or updated |
| Erasure | Their data deleted (unless you must keep it by law) |
| Grievance | A complaint about how their data was handled |
| Nomination | Someone to exercise their rights if they die or can't act |
| Consent withdrawal | To stop processing based on their consent |

## Due dates

Each request gets two dates:

- **Due**: the date of receipt plus your own service level, set in **Settings → Organisation** (default 30 days);
- **Legal limit**: 90 days after receipt, the most the DPDP Rules allow for responding to grievances. Your service level can never exceed it.

The assignee (or the admins, if nobody is assigned) is reminded 3 days before the due date, and again when a request becomes overdue; overdue requests are also posted to Slack or Teams. Upcoming due dates also appear on the [Dashboard](/docs/dashboard).

## Handling a request

1. **Log a rights request** (for requests by email, phone or letter): type, requester name and email, details, channel and received time, and an assignee. Requests from the public page are created automatically.
2. **Verify identity** before sharing or changing anything, then tick **Identity verified**. Ask only for what you need to confirm it's them.
3. Move the status through **New → Verifying → In progress → Completed** (or **Rejected**, with the legal reason).
4. Record the **resolution**: what you did and what you told the person. This is your evidence for PRV-10.

Use the [data inventory](/docs/data-inventory) to find where the person's data lives, and [consent records](/docs/consent-records) to see their consent history.

## The public privacy request page

DPDP expects an easy way for people to contact you. Turn on a public page in **Settings → Privacy request page**:

- set the **page address**, for example `https://app.yourcompany.com/p/your-company`;
- add your **privacy contact name and email** (your Grievance Officer or DPO), which are shown on the page;
- tick **Page is live**.

Link to it from your privacy notice, website footer and app settings. Someone filling in the form must **confirm their email address** through a link before the request is created, which filters out spam and gives you a verified contact. Submissions are rate-limited.

/help/incidents.title: Incidents and breaches
/help/incidents.summary: Report incidents from the dashboard, track them by email in one thread per incident, run the CERT-In 6-hour and DPDP Board clocks, then investigate and learn.
/help/incidents.body_md:
When something goes wrong, the clock starts at once. **Incidents** records what happened, starts the right regulatory clocks, and keeps the whole response in one record.

## Reporting an incident

Anyone in your organisation except auditors can report an incident, from two places:

- **Report incident** at the top of the **Dashboard**, so it's one click away for everyone;
- **Report incident** on the **Incidents** page.

Report as soon as you notice something, even if you're not sure it's serious: the CERT-In clock is only 6 hours. Fill in:

- **What happened** and **Details**: what you saw, which systems or data are involved, and anything you've already done. Don't paste passwords or customers' personal data;
- **Noticed at (IST)**: when you first became aware; all clocks run from this time;
- **How serious does it look?**: SEV-3 (suspicious, not sure yet), SEV-2 (likely compromise, limited impact) or SEV-1 (confirmed breach or major outage);
- **Category** (optional): for example phishing, lost device, data leak, ransomware;
- **Personal data may be involved**: tick if anyone's personal data may have been seen, copied, changed or lost. This starts the DPDP clock. If unsure, tick it; the incident lead can change it;
- **Reportable to CERT-In**: tick for incident types in the CERT-In Directions, such as unauthorised access, system compromise, data leaks, ransomware or attacks on servers and cloud accounts;
- **Incident lead** (admins only).

As soon as you report, admins are alerted by email (and on Slack or Teams, if connected), with the clocks that are running, and you get a confirmation email.

## Tracking by email

Every incident has its own **email thread**. The first email's subject is the incident number and title, for example **INC-7: Phishing email clicked**, and every later email uses the same subject and is sent as a reply. So the whole incident, from the report to closure, sits in one conversation in your inbox.

**Who gets the emails (followers):** the person who reported it, the incident lead, and your organisation's owners and admins. Whoever becomes lead is added automatically. Anyone who can see the incident can choose **Follow by email**, or **Stop email updates**, on the incident page. If nobody follows an incident, admins still get the emails.

**What's emailed:**

| Event | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Reported | Who reported it, the details and the clocks running |
| Update posted | The text of the update |
| Status changed | Open → Contained; on closing, the root cause, actions and lessons |
| Severity changed | SEV-2 → SEV-1 |
| Lead assigned | "Meera is now the incident lead." |
| Classification changed | Marked as a personal data breach or CERT-In reportable, which starts a clock |
| Regulatory report recorded | "Reported to CERT-In at 14:05 IST" |
| Deadline reminders | CERT-In 2 hours before and overdue; Board report 24 hours before and overdue |

You don't get an email about your own changes. Edits to long text, such as root cause or details, are recorded on the timeline but not emailed. Replies to these emails aren't added to the incident: post updates on the incident page so they're recorded and everyone sees them.

## Timeline and updates

The incident page shows a **Timeline** of everything that happened, newest first: the report, updates, status and severity changes, the lead, classifications, regulatory reports and edits, each with who and when. Use **Post an update** to record what you found, what you did and what happens next. Updates are emailed to followers.

The timeline can't be edited or deleted, so it's a reliable record for regulators and auditors.

## The regulatory clocks

| Clock | Starts when | Due | Reminders |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CERT-In report | Reportable to CERT-In is ticked | 6 hours after the incident was noticed | 2 hours before, and when overdue |
| Data Protection Board detailed report | Personal data breach is ticked | 72 hours after the incident was noticed | 24 hours before, and when overdue |
| Notifying affected people | Personal data breach is ticked | Without delay | Shown on the dashboard until recorded |

Record each report as you make it under **Regulatory reporting**: CERT-In reported at, Board initial report at, Board detailed report at, people notified at. A clock stops when its time is recorded. The initial report to the Board is also due without delay; record when you sent it, even though it has no countdown. The dashboard shows every running clock with its countdown.

## Financial regulator clocks

If you're regulated by the RBI, SEBI, IRDAI or IFSCA, the incident form and incident page show **Reportable to RBI** (or SEBI, IRDAI, IFSCA). These options appear when you use one of that regulator's frameworks. Ticking one adds its clocks:

| Regulator | Clock | Due |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RBI | Report to RBI on the DAKSH portal (non-bank PSOs use the Annex 1 format; housing finance companies report to NHB) | 6 hours after detection |
| SEBI | Report to SEBI through its portal (CSCRF) | 6 hours after detection |
| IRDAI | Copy the CERT-In report to IRDAI | 6 hours after detection |
| IFSCA | Initial report, interim report, root cause analysis | 6 hours, 3 days and 30 days after detection |

Each clock has **Mark done now** and can be corrected later. Reminders go to the incident's followers 2 hours before a 6-hour clock (a day before longer ones) and when overdue, in the incident's email thread, and running clocks appear in the dashboard's deadlines.

> CERT-In reports go to incident@cert-in.org.in using their reporting format; breach reports go to the Data Protection Board. The platform tracks the deadlines and keeps the record; it doesn't submit reports for you.

## Investigating and closing

Move the status through **Open → Contained → Resolved → Closed**, and fill in the **Investigation** section:

- **Root cause**: why it happened;
- **Actions taken**: containment and fixes;
- **Lessons learned**: what changes to prevent a repeat. Turn them into tasks.

A closed incident with root cause and lessons is the evidence auditors look for under INC-04 (post-incident review). Keep logs and other evidence preserved (INC-05) and attach them to the related controls.

## Practise

Run a tabletop exercise at least once a year: record a realistic scenario as an incident (mark it as an exercise in the title) and walk through the clocks. It's evidence for INC-01.

/help/risk-register.title: Risk register
/help/risk-register.summary: Record, score and treat risks, link them to the controls that reduce them, and track treatment in Jira.
/help/risk-register.body_md:
A risk register lists the things that could go wrong, how likely and how bad they'd be, and what you're doing about them. ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, HIPAA and the RBI and SEBI frameworks all require one (RISK-01, RISK-02).

## Adding a risk

**Add risk** and fill in:

| Field | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| Risk | A specific event with a consequence: "Customer data exposed through a misconfigured storage bucket", not "Cloud security" |
| Description | Causes, affected assets and what would happen |
| Category | For example Privacy, Cloud, People, Vendor, Compliance |
| Likelihood | 1 (rare) to 5 (almost certain) |
| Impact | 1 (minor) to 5 (severe) |
| Treatment | **Mitigate** (reduce it with controls), **Accept** (live with it, approved by the owner), **Transfer** (insurance or contract) or **Avoid** (stop the activity) |
| Status | Open, Treated or Closed |
| Treatment plan | What you're doing, by when |
| Linked controls | The controls that reduce this risk |
| Owner and review date | Who's accountable, and when to look at it again |

## Scoring

**Score = likelihood × impact**, from 1 to 25:

| Score | Level |
| --- | --- |
| 15 to 25 | High |
| 8 to 14 | Medium |
| 1 to 7 | Low |

The **heat map** shows open risks by likelihood and impact; the register lists them highest first. Write down how much risk you're willing to accept (your risk appetite) and treat everything above it.

## A good first register

Start with ten to fifteen risks covering: account takeover through phishing, ransomware on laptops, cloud misconfiguration exposing data, a key vendor breach, insider misuse of customer data, missed CERT-In or DPDP deadlines, loss of a critical person, a production outage without a working backup, payment fraud through business email compromise, and vulnerable code reaching production. The demo companies include examples.

## Jira

With [Jira](/docs/jira) connected, every new risk gets a Jira issue automatically (summary, score, treatment plan and linked controls), edits are pushed to it, and the issue's status comes back: **Done** marks the risk **treated**, and reopening it sets it back to **open**. Risks your team logs in Jira can be imported too. Use **Sync with Jira** to sync straight away, or **Create issue** for a risk added before Jira was connected.

## Reviewing

Review the register at least yearly and after major changes or incidents. The review itself is evidence; note the date and decisions, and update review dates.

/help/vendors.title: Vendors
/help/vendors.summary: Your vendor inventory - risk tiers, data processing agreements, certificates with expiry tracking, reviews and security questionnaires.
/help/vendors.body_md:
Your vendors are part of your security: a breach at your payroll provider or cloud host is your problem too. DPDP makes you responsible for what your processors do with personal data, and every framework asks you to assess suppliers (VEN-01 to VEN-03).

## Adding a vendor

**Add vendor** and record:

| Field | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| Name, website, services | What they do for you |
| Risk tier | **Critical**: you can't operate without them, or they hold sensitive data at scale. **High**: access to confidential or personal data. **Medium**: limited access. **Low**: no access to your data or systems. |
| Data shared | Categories of data they get |
| Processes personal data | Tick if they're a DPDP data processor |
| DPA signed | Whether a data processing agreement is in place |
| Data location | Where they store your data |
| Certifications | ISO 27001, SOC 2 and so on |
| Status | Onboarding, Active or Offboarded |
| Owner, last assessed, next review | Who manages the relationship, and the review cycle |

When you mark a vendor's questionnaire as reviewed, the next review date is set by tier: critical and high vendors every 12 months, medium every 24 months, low vendors none. You can also set the date yourself. When a review falls due, a **Review vendor** task is created, and vendors due in the next 30 days show on the dashboard.

## Certificates and documents

On a vendor's page, upload documents with a **type** and **valid until** date: ISO 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report, data processing agreement, penetration test summary, cyber insurance or other. Vendors can also upload them while answering a questionnaire. The platform emails a reminder before a document expires and when it has expired.

## Security questionnaires

Send questionnaires from the vendor's page with **Send questionnaire**. The vendor answers through a secure link, without an account. The platform scores the answers, highlights critical gaps, reminds the vendor and records your review as evidence. See [Vendor questionnaires](/docs/vendor-questionnaires).

## Offboarding

When you stop using a vendor, set the status to **Offboarded**, get confirmation that your data was returned or deleted, upload that confirmation, and remove their access.

/help/vendor-questionnaires.summary: The questionnaire library, sending core and add-on questionnaires, the vendor's experience, scoring, reminders, review and customising your own.
/help/vendor-questionnaires.body_md:
A security questionnaire asks a vendor how they protect your data. The platform includes industry-standard questionnaires, sends them by secure link, scores the answers and keeps everything as evidence.

## The library

**Vendors → Questionnaires → Questionnaire library**.

### Core questionnaires: send one to every vendor

| Questionnaire | Questions | Recommended for |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Standard security questionnaire (Full) | 96 in 18 domains | High and critical vendors |
| Standard security questionnaire (Lite) | 47 | Medium vendors |
| Quick security baseline | 26 | Low-risk vendors |

The Full questionnaire covers company and governance; policies and risk; compliance and assurance; people; assets and data; identity and access; application security; infrastructure and network; cloud; endpoints; vulnerability management; logging and monitoring; incident management; business continuity; physical security; subprocessors; privacy; and AI. Questions are referenced to ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2, so vendors can answer from their existing audit material. The Lite set uses the same question IDs, so answers stay comparable if you later send the Full set.

These are written in-house in the structure of common industry questionnaires; they don't reproduce SIG or CAIQ. If you have a SIG licence, import it from Excel (see below).

### Add-ons: send alongside a core questionnaire when relevant

| Add-on | Questions | When |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| DPDP Data Processor | 14 | The vendor processes personal data for you (pre-selected for processors) |
| GDPR processor (Article 28) | 12 | The vendor processes personal data of people in the EU or UK |
| AI and machine learning vendor | 14 | The service uses AI on your data or supplies AI models |
| Payment card data (PCI DSS) | 9 | Payment gateways and anyone handling card data |

**View questions** shows every question with its type, expected answer, weight and references. **Excel** downloads any questionnaire.

## Sending

1. On a vendor's page, **Send questionnaire**.
2. The core questionnaire matching the vendor's tier is pre-selected; tick any add-ons. The total question count is shown.
3. Enter the vendor contact's email and the number of days until it's due (3 to 60, default 21).
4. **Send**. The vendor gets one email with a link per questionnaire. You can copy the links too.

## What the vendor sees

A secure page, no account needed, with each question grouped by section and guidance where useful. They can:

- answer Yes, No or N/A, choose from a list, or write text;
- add a comment to any answer (and must explain every N/A on a scored question);
- upload certificates and reports;
- save and come back before submitting.

Links work only until the due date and can't be guessed. Anyone with the link can answer, so send it only to the vendor's security contact.

## Tracking: Sent to vendors

**Sent to vendors** lists every questionnaire you've sent, with tiles for **Waiting for vendor**, **Ready to review**, **Expired** and **Reviewed**, search and filters. Each row shows progress (answered out of total) or the score.

- **Remind**: emails the vendor again with a **fresh link** (old links stop working) and extends the due date if it's close. You can remind at most once every 12 hours.
- **Automatic reminder**: sent 3 days before the due date if the vendor hasn't submitted.
- **Cancel**: stops the link working.
- **Download**: the answers as Excel.

## Scoring

Each yes/no question has an expected answer and a weight from 0 to 3. Weight 3 means **critical**.

- **Score** = weight of answers matching the expected answer ÷ total weight answered (N/A answers are left out), from 0 to 100.
- **Risk rating**: 85 or more is low, 65 to 84 medium, below 65 high. A wrong answer to any critical question means the rating can't be better than medium.
- Critical gaps are highlighted for the reviewer.

## Reviewing

Open a submitted questionnaire to see the score, rating, critical gaps and every answer, with answers below expectation highlighted (**Show only gaps** narrows the list). Add **review notes** (accepted risks and follow-ups) and **Mark reviewed**. The review is attached as evidence to **VEN-01 Vendor risk management**.

## Your own questionnaires

- **Duplicate to customise** any built-in questionnaire, then add, remove, reorder and edit questions.
- **New questionnaire** starts from scratch.
- **Import from Excel or CSV**: columns Section, Question, Type (Yes/No, Text or Choice), Weight (0 to 3), Expected answer, Evidence required and Options (separated by |). Only Question is required. Formulas in the file are never evaluated.

For each question set the section, type, expected answer, weight and whether to ask for evidence; choice questions need their options. Questionnaires already sent keep their own copy of the questions, so later edits never change what a vendor answered. Exports neutralise spreadsheet formulas in vendor answers, so a malicious answer can't run in Excel.

/help/introduction.title: Introduction
/help/introduction.summary: What the platform does, how its parts fit together, and what is automated versus what your team does.
/help/introduction.body_md:
Pramaanly is a compliance automation platform built for Indian companies first. It helps you get and stay compliant with India's **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act**, the **CERT-In Directions**, sector rules from **RBI** and **SEBI**, and international standards such as **ISO 27001**, **SOC 2**, **NIST CSF**, **PCI DSS**, **GDPR** and **HIPAA**. It does this from one place, with one set of work.

If you have never done compliance before, read this page and [Key concepts](/docs/concepts). They explain the few ideas everything else builds on.

## What the platform does for you

Compliance work usually means four things, and the platform covers each of them:

1. **Knowing what you must do.** Each framework is broken into requirements, written in plain language. The platform turns those into a single list of **controls**: concrete things your company does, such as "MFA is enforced for everyone" or "access is reviewed every quarter".
2. **Doing it and proving it.** For each control you record how it works and attach **evidence** (a screenshot, an export, a signed document). Where you connect your systems (AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub and 22 others), the evidence is collected automatically and checked every few hours.
3. **Running the ongoing operations.** Policies with approval and staff acknowledgment, security training and phishing tests, access reviews, vendor due diligence, the risk register, and the DPDP operations: data inventory, consent records, rights requests and breach handling.
4. **Passing the audit.** Auditors get their own time-limited accounts to request evidence, test samples, and download a verified evidence pack and Statement of Applicability.

## How the parts fit together

~~~
Frameworks (DPDP, ISO 27001, SOC 2 …)
   └─ Requirements (e.g. ISO 27001 A.5.17 "Authentication information")
        └─ mapped to Controls (e.g. ACC-08 "Password and secrets management")
             ├─ Evidence: files, links, notes, automated check results
             ├─ Owner, status and review frequency
             └─ Tasks when something needs doing
                  ↓
           Control health  →  Framework readiness %
~~~

The important design choice: **one control can satisfy many frameworks**. Enforcing MFA counts for DPDP, ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, PCI DSS and HIPAA at once, so you do the work once. When you turn on a new framework, the platform adds only the controls you don't have yet.

## What is automated and what isn't

| Automated by the platform | Done by your team, made easy by the platform |
| --- | --- |
| Checks from 25 integrations, every 6 hours, with evidence saved automatically | Writing and approving policies (templates, upload, or AI drafts) |
| Failing checks turned into tasks and alerts | Deciding how each control works in your company |
| Reminders for expiring evidence, overdue tasks, legal deadlines | Uploading evidence that no system can provide (minutes, signed forms) |
| Leaver checks: people who left but still have accounts | Reviewing and approving evidence uploaded by others |
| Training assignment, reminders, phishing simulations and the HR-03 check | Taking training; responding to incidents and rights requests |
| CERT-In 6-hour and DPDP Board clocks on incidents | Making risk and vendor decisions |
| Vendor questionnaire sending, scoring and reminders | Working with your auditor |
| Automatic checks on uploaded evidence, and an optional AI check | |

The **Automation coverage** panel on the [Integrations](/docs/integrations) page shows how much of your control set runs itself, and what to connect next.

## Who uses it

| Role | Typical person | What they do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner | Founder, CEO or CTO | Everything, including billing-level decisions such as turning on AI and single sign-on |
| Admin | Head of security, compliance lead | Runs the programme: settings, approvals, assignments, integrations |
| Member | Engineers, HR, finance, managers | Owns controls, uploads evidence, completes tasks and training |
| Auditor | External auditor (time-limited) | Reads everything, raises evidence requests, tests samples |

See [Roles and permissions](/docs/roles-and-permissions) for the full list.

## Where to go next

- [Your first 30 days](/docs/first-steps): a practical plan from sign-up to audit-ready.
- [Key concepts](/docs/concepts): control health, readiness and evidence validity explained.
- [Frameworks](/docs/frameworks): which frameworks apply to you.

/help/first-steps.title: Your first 30 days
/help/first-steps.summary: A week-by-week plan from sign-up to a programme that runs itself and is ready for an auditor.
/help/first-steps.body_md:
This plan assumes a company of 20 to 300 people starting from scratch. Smaller companies can move faster; the order stays the same.

## Day 1: set up the workspace

1. **Sign up and confirm your email.** The person who signs up becomes the **owner**.
2. **Complete onboarding.** Pick your sector; the platform suggests frameworks (for example DPDP, CERT-In, ISO 27001 and SOC 2 for B2B SaaS). Answer the short profile questions; they switch on extra requirements only when they apply, such as children's data under DPDP or card terminals under PCI DSS. You can change all of this later in **Settings**.
3. **Turn on two-step verification** for yourself under **Account security**, then require it for everyone under **Settings → Security**. Auditors will ask.
4. **Invite your admin** (the person who will run compliance day to day) and the people who own systems: engineering lead, IT, HR, finance.

## Week 1: connect your systems

Integrations do the most work for the least effort, so do them first.

1. Open **Integrations**. The **Connect next** panel lists the integrations that would automate the most controls for you.
2. Connect your identity provider first (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365 or Okta), then your cloud (AWS, Azure or Google Cloud), your code host (GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket) and your device management tool.
3. Connect your HR system (Keka, Darwinbox, greytHR or Zoho People), or upload the HR roster as a CSV on the **People & accounts** page. This powers leaver checks, access reviews and training.
4. After the first sync, open **Controls** and filter by **Failing check**. Each failing check has a task explaining what to fix.

Every connector is read-only, except Jira, which creates issues if you ask it to. See [Integrations](/docs/integrations).

## Week 2: assign owners and write policies

1. In **Controls**, tick the controls for each area and use **Assign** to give them owners in bulk. Owners get an email.
2. In **Policies**, choose **New policy**. Upload your existing policies (Word, PDF or pasted from Google Docs), or start from the templates. Approve them; every approved policy is attached as evidence to the controls it supports, and staff are asked to acknowledge it.
3. In **Training**, check which courses are required. The three foundation courses are on by default; add role-based ones such as Secure development for Engineering.

## Week 3: fill the evidence gaps

1. Open **Controls** and filter by **Needs evidence**.
2. For each control, read **What the evidence must show** and add the evidence that shows those points. Each upload is checked automatically for common problems.
3. Someone other than the uploader reviews each item in **Evidence review**. Only approved evidence counts.
4. Mark controls that genuinely don't apply as **Not applicable**, with a reason.

## Week 4: run the operations once

1. Start your first **access review** from **Access reviews**. Managers confirm or remove each account.
2. Add your vendors in **Vendors**, set their risk tier and send each high-risk vendor a security questionnaire.
3. Fill the **Risk register** with your top ten risks and their treatment.
4. Fill the **Data inventory** (DPDP record of processing). Use **Data discovery** to find personal data in your databases.
5. Publish your consent notices and connect your website or app to the [Consent API](/docs/api#consent-api).
6. Run a **phishing simulation** to get a baseline.

## After 30 days: keep it running

The platform now tells you what needs doing:

- **Dashboard**: deadlines, controls that need attention and your tasks.
- **Tasks**: created automatically when a check fails, evidence is about to expire, a review is due or a vendor needs reassessing.
- **Alerts** by email, Slack or Teams for failing checks and legal deadlines (set up in **Settings → Notifications**).

When your readiness for a framework is above about 90%, invite your auditor with an **Auditor** account and work through the [Audit workspace](/docs/audit-workspace).

/help/concepts.title: Key concepts
/help/concepts.summary: Frameworks, requirements, controls, evidence, control health and readiness, and the rules that connect them.
/help/concepts.body_md:
Everything in the platform builds on a few ideas. Once you know them, the screens explain themselves.

## Frameworks and requirements

A **framework** is a law, regulation or standard: the DPDP Act, ISO 27001, SOC 2 and so on. Each framework is made of **requirements**, such as "ISO 27001 A.8.13 Information backup" or "DPDP s.8(5) Reasonable security safeguards". The platform shows each requirement with plain-language guidance. Where the source is copyrighted (ISO, AICPA, PCI SSC), the official text is not reproduced; you get the identifier and our guidance.

Some requirements only apply in certain situations; for example, DPDP's children's data rules apply only if you process children's data. These are **conditional requirements**. They switch on when you answer the matching profile question in onboarding or **Settings → Organisation**, and otherwise drop out of your scores.

## Controls

A **control** is something your company does that meets one or more requirements, for example "ACC-03 Multi-factor authentication". The platform ships a library of 110 controls, each mapped to every requirement it helps meet across all 11 frameworks. Turning on a framework adds the controls it needs that you don't already have.

Each control has:

- an **owner**: the person responsible for it;
- an **implementation status**: Not started, In progress, Implemented or Not applicable (with a written reason);
- a **review frequency**: continuous, monthly, quarterly, every 6 months, yearly or once; this sets how long evidence stays valid;
- **what the evidence must show**: two or three specific points a reviewer or auditor checks;
- **evidence** and **tasks**.

You can add your own **custom controls**, and edit the title, description, category, frequency and evidence criteria of any control.

## Evidence

**Evidence** proves a control works. It comes in five kinds:

| Kind | Example | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automated | "Root account has MFA enabled: pass" | An integration check or the evidence API |
| Policy | An approved access control policy | Approving a policy in the platform |
| File | A screenshot, PDF, export or spreadsheet | Uploaded by a person |
| Link | A Confluence page or Google Drive document | Added by a person |
| Note | "We do this by…" | Written by a person |

Every item has a **valid until** date. By default it is one review cycle from when it was added: for example 92 days for a quarterly control or 366 days for a yearly one. Evidence uploaded by people also has to be **approved by a second person** before it counts. See [Evidence](/docs/evidence).

## How control health works

Each control gets a **health** status, worked out in this order:

1. **Not applicable**: you marked it N/A with a reason. It is excluded from scores.
2. **Failing check**: any automated check mapped to it is currently failing. This wins over everything else, because a live system says the control is broken.
3. **Passing**: the control is marked Implemented and has at least one item of approved evidence that hasn't expired.
4. **Needs evidence**: the control is marked Implemented but has no current approved evidence. Evidence waiting for review shows as "awaiting review" but doesn't count yet.
5. **In progress** or **Not started**: otherwise, the control's implementation status.

## How readiness is calculated

For each framework you have turned on:

- a requirement is **met** when every control mapped to it is Passing or Not applicable;
- it is **partly met** when some of its controls are passing or in progress;
- it is **not met** otherwise;
- requirements whose condition doesn't apply to you are left out.

**Readiness %** = met requirements ÷ applicable requirements. Because controls are shared, improving one control can raise several frameworks at once.

## Tasks

A **task** is a piece of work with an assignee and due date. You can create tasks yourself, but most are created automatically:

- a check failed (the task closes itself when the check passes again);
- evidence for an implemented control is missing, or expires within 14 days;
- a policy, vendor review or quarterly access review is due;
- an access review decided an account must be removed.

## The audit trail

Every change (a status update, an upload, a download, an approval, a settings change) is written to a tamper-evident **audit log**. Each entry is chained to the previous one with a hash, so any later alteration is detectable. Admins can view and verify it in **Settings → Audit log**.

/help/roles-and-permissions.title: Roles and permissions
/help/roles-and-permissions.summary: What owners, admins, members and auditors can see and do, and how to invite and manage people.
/help/roles-and-permissions.body_md:
Every person in an organisation has one of four roles. A person can belong to several organisations (for example a consultant or group company) and switch between them from the organisation menu at the top of the sidebar.

## The four roles

| | Owner | Admin | Member | Auditor |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| See everything in the workspace | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (read-only) |
| Update controls, upload evidence, manage tasks, risks, vendors, DPDP records | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| Own controls and policies | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| Review (approve or send back) uploaded evidence | ✓ | ✓ | Only for controls they own | |
| Approve and delete policies | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| Invite people, change roles, remove members | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| Connect integrations, manage settings, notifications and API keys | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| Manage training assignments, company courses and phishing simulations | ✓ | ✓ | | |
| Raise evidence requests, accept or reject submitted evidence | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Draw evidence samples and record test results | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Download the evidence pack and requirements matrix | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Turn the AI assistant and AI evidence checks on or off | ✓ | | | |
| Configure single sign-on | ✓ | | | |

Nobody can approve evidence they uploaded themselves while someone else is able to; see [Evidence review](/docs/evidence-review).

## Owner

The person who creates the organisation is its owner. Owners have every admin right plus a few decisions that affect data sharing or sign-in for everyone: the AI assistant, AI evidence checks and single sign-on. When single sign-on is enforced, owners can still sign in with their password and two-step verification as break-glass access.

## Admin

Admins run the compliance programme. Most organisations have one or two.

## Member

Members do the day-to-day work: they own controls, add evidence, complete tasks and training, and handle DPDP requests and incidents. Use the member role for anyone who isn't running the programme.

## Auditor

The auditor role is for external auditors and assessors. Auditors:

- can see every control, policy, piece of evidence and record, but can't change any of them;
- have **time-limited access**: you choose how many days (1 to 365) when you invite them, and access ends automatically; a banner shows them the end date;
- work in the [Audit workspace](/docs/audit-workspace): they raise evidence requests, accept or reject what your team submits, test samples, and download exports;
- can't own controls or policies, and can't review evidence.

## Inviting people

**Settings → Team → Invite someone.** Enter the email address and role. For auditors, also set the number of days of access. The invitation link is valid for 7 days. You must have confirmed your own email address before you can invite others.

People from your HR roster who don't have an account can be invited in one go from **Training → Team progress → Invite them**, so they can take their training.

## Changing or removing access

In **Settings → Team**, change a member's role or remove them. Removing someone takes away their access to the organisation straight away. Their past work (evidence, approvals, audit log entries) keeps their name.

If you use single sign-on with just-in-time provisioning, new people from your verified domains get an account with the default role (member or auditor) the first time they sign in. See [Sign-in and security settings](/docs/sign-in-security).

/help/evidence.title: Evidence
/help/evidence.summary: The kinds of evidence, how to add it well, how long it stays valid, and the automatic checks and fingerprints that protect it.
/help/evidence.body_md:
Evidence is what an auditor looks at to decide whether a control works. The platform makes it easy to add, checks it automatically, has a second person approve it, and proves it hasn't been changed.

## Kinds of evidence and how much auditors trust them

Every evidence item is labelled with where it came from:

| Label | Kinds | Examples | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Collected automatically** | Automated | "All RDS instances are encrypted at rest: pass" | Taken straight from your systems, so no one could pick or edit it. Approved automatically. |
| **Generated in the platform** | Policy, access review, vendor assessment, training report | An approved policy; a signed-off access review | Produced by a workflow with its own approvals. Approved automatically. |
| **Uploaded** | File, link, note | A screenshot, PDF, spreadsheet, Confluence link or written note | Chosen by a person, so it's checked and needs a second person's approval. |

Automate where you can: each control's **Collect automatically** panel shows which integrations could provide its evidence.

## Adding evidence

On a control, click **Add evidence** and choose:

- **File**: PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, JSON, text, YAML or ZIP, up to 25 MB;
- **Link**: a URL to where the evidence lives (make sure the auditor will be able to open it);
- **Note**: a written statement. A note says something happens but doesn't prove it, so use it alongside a record wherever possible.

Then:

1. Give it a clear title, such as "Q3 2026 access review: AWS and GitHub".
2. Tick **This evidence shows** for each point from **What the evidence must show** that this item proves. Other evidence can cover the remaining points.
3. Optionally set **Valid until**. Otherwise it's one review cycle (see [Controls](/docs/controls#review-frequency)).

After saving you'll see the result of the automatic checks straight away. If they found a problem with the wrong file, delete it and upload the right one.

### What makes evidence good

- **Dated** within the current review period, with the date visible (in a screenshot, include the clock or a date on the page).
- **Specific**: shows your organisation's account, tenant or name.
- **Complete**: the filled-in, approved document, not the template.
- **Shows it working**, not just a rule: a policy says MFA is required; a screenshot of the identity provider's MFA enforcement setting proves it.
- **Covers every point** in What the evidence must show, across one or more items.

## What the evidence must show

Each of the 110 controls has two or three acceptance criteria, for example for ACC-03 Multi-factor authentication:

1. MFA is enforced (not just available) for all users in the identity provider.
2. MFA is enforced for cloud console and administrator access.
3. The screenshot or report shows the date or was exported within the review period.

The control page shows each point with a tick when approved evidence covers it, a dashed circle when evidence awaiting review covers it, and an empty circle when nothing covers it yet. A point counts as covered when the uploader confirms it or the AI check finds it, and a reviewer approves the evidence. Admins can change a control's criteria with **Edit**.

## Automatic checks

Every new evidence item is checked straight away. Warnings don't block anything; they tell the uploader and reviewer what to look at.

| Check | What it catches |
| --- | --- |
| Reused file | The exact same file was uploaded to this control in an earlier review period. Evidence should show the control working now. |
| Duplicate or shared file | The same file is already on this control, or on other controls (fine for a policy covering several controls). |
| Outdated document | The PDF or Office document's own date is before the review period starts. |
| Future date | The document is dated in the future. |
| Unfinished template | Placeholders such as [Company Name], [Insert date], {{name}}, TBD or lorem ipsum. |
| Very little text | A document with under 25 words. |
| Unreadable | Scanned PDFs, password-protected PDFs and old .doc/.xls files can't be read automatically; the reviewer must open them. |
| Screenshot reminder | Screenshots should show the date and the account they come from. |
| Note only | A note is a statement, not proof. |
| Broken link | Links are opened (safely) when added and re-checked weekly; "not found" and errors are flagged, and links that need a sign-in are noted so you can make sure the auditor has access. |

Click the **run checks again** icon on an item to re-run them, for example after changing a control's criteria.

If your owner has turned it on, the [AI evidence check](/docs/evidence-review#ai-evidence-check) also reads the file and gives a verdict.

## Fingerprints: proving evidence hasn't changed

When a file is uploaded, the platform calculates its **SHA-256 fingerprint**, a code that changes completely if even one byte of the file changes, before encrypting and storing it. Then:

- every download recalculates the fingerprint; if it no longer matches, the download is refused and the event is logged;
- the [evidence pack](/docs/audit-workspace#evidence-pack) records each file's upload-time fingerprint and whether the file is unchanged;
- auditor samples record the fingerprint, so a file changed after it was sampled is flagged.

Files added before fingerprints existed are fingerprinted by the background worker, marked with the date it happened.

## Expiry and renewal

Evidence counts only until its **valid until** date. When it expires, the control drops to **Needs evidence**. Fourteen days before that, the owner gets a **Renew evidence** task. Automated evidence is refreshed on every successful sync, so it doesn't expire while the integration is connected.

## Deleting evidence

Uploaded evidence can be deleted from the control page. Automated and policy evidence can't be deleted: it is managed by the integration or policy. Every deletion is recorded in the audit log.

/help/phishing-simulations.title: Phishing simulations
/help/phishing-simulations.summary: Send safe test phishing emails to your own staff, measure who clicks, teach in the moment and enrol clickers in training.
/help/phishing-simulations.body_md:
A phishing simulation sends a realistic but harmless test email to your staff. People who click see a short lesson on what they missed. Over time, click rates fall, and you have evidence for awareness controls.

## Safety by design

- Emails go **only to your own company's email domains** (your verified domains and your admins' domains). Personal addresses such as Gmail are skipped automatically.
- Emails are sent **from the platform's own address**, with a display name such as "IT Helpdesk". They never spoof your domain or a real brand.
- The landing page **collects nothing**: no passwords, no form fields. It records only that the link was opened.
- **Link scanners don't count as clicks.** Email security gateways open links automatically; a click is recorded only when the page loads in a real browser.
- Individual results are visible to **admins only**. Use them to coach, not to blame.

## Templates

| Template | Difficulty | Pretends to be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Password expires today | Easy | IT Helpdesk |
| Missed delivery | Easy | Courier |
| Shared document | Medium | File sharing |
| Overdue invoice | Medium | Accounts receivable |
| UPI refund | Medium | Payments team |
| HR policy acknowledgement | Hard | HR team |
| Urgent request from leadership | Hard | Office of the CEO |

Each template comes with the warning signs people should have noticed, shown on the lesson page and in the results.

## Running a simulation

1. **Training → Phishing simulations → New simulation**.
2. Name it, pick a template (a preview is shown), and choose departments, or leave them all unticked to send to everyone.
3. Decide whether to **assign the phishing course to anyone who clicks** (on by default; due in 14 days).
4. **Save as draft**. The draft shows how many people it will go to.
5. Before launching, ask IT to **allow-list the platform's sending address** so the emails aren't filtered, and let leadership know a test is running.
6. **Launch**. Emails are sent in the background.
7. Watch results come in: delivered, clicked, click rate overall and by department, and each person's result.
8. **Close** the simulation when you're done; later clicks are no longer counted.

Sent simulations are kept as training evidence and can't be deleted, only closed.

## What people see when they click

A page titled **This was a phishing simulation**, explaining that nothing happened and no information was collected, the email they clicked, what should have made them pause, three habits for next time, and a link to the phishing course if they were enrolled.

## Good practice

- Run one every quarter, increasing the difficulty as click rates fall.
- Vary templates; people share what they saw.
- Celebrate reporting: people who report suspicious emails quickly are your best defence.

/help/dpdp-overview.title: DPDP at a glance
/help/dpdp-overview.summary: What India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act asks of you, its deadlines, and which part of the platform handles each duty.
/help/dpdp-overview.body_md:
The **Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023** and the **DPDP Rules, 2025** govern how organisations handle digital personal data in India. The platform covers the Act as a framework (49 requirements) and gives you working tools for the duties that need day-to-day operations.

> This page explains the platform, not the law. For legal advice on your situation, speak to a privacy lawyer.

## Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Data Principal | The person the data is about: your customer, user or employee |
| Data Fiduciary | You: the organisation deciding why and how data is processed |
| Data Processor | A vendor processing data on your behalf (cloud host, email provider, payroll) |
| Significant Data Fiduciary (SDF) | A fiduciary notified by the government for extra duties (DPO in India, audits, DPIAs) |
| Consent Manager | A registered intermediary through which people can give, manage and withdraw consent |
| Data Protection Board (DPB) | The regulator that receives breach reports and handles complaints |

## Your main duties and where to handle them

| Duty | Platform module |
| --- | --- |
| Know what personal data you process, why, on what basis and with whom | [Data inventory](/docs/data-inventory) |
| Find personal data you didn't know about | [Data discovery](/docs/data-discovery) |
| Give a clear notice and get valid consent; make withdrawal as easy | [Consent records](/docs/consent-records) |
| Respond to access, correction, erasure, nomination, withdrawal and grievance requests | [Rights requests](/docs/rights-requests) |
| Report personal data breaches to the Board and tell affected people | [Incidents](/docs/incidents) |
| Have reasonable security safeguards | The security controls across [Controls](/docs/controls) |
| Bind processors by contract and check them | [Vendors](/docs/vendors) and the DPDP processor questionnaire |
| Keep data only as long as needed | PRV-08 Retention and erasure, and the retention field in the inventory |
| Train staff | The "India's DPDP Act for everyone at work" course in [Training](/docs/training) |

## Phased start dates

The DPDP Rules come into force in phases: the Data Protection Board from 13 November 2025, Consent Manager provisions from 13 November 2026, and the remaining obligations from 13 May 2027. The DPDP framework page in the platform shows the requirements with this context.

## Deadlines the platform tracks

| Deadline | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Personal data breach: report to the Board without delay, with a detailed report within 72 hours | Incident clocks and the dashboard |
| Rights requests: within your own service level, never more than 90 days | Rights request due dates |
| CERT-In (a separate law, often triggered by the same incident): report within 6 hours | Incident clocks |

## DPDP-specific profile questions

Answer these in **Settings → Organisation → What applies to you** to switch on the matching requirements: processing children's data, being a Significant Data Fiduciary, and using a Consent Manager. See [Frameworks](/docs/frameworks#conditional-requirements-and-profile-questions).

/help/jira.title: Jira
/help/jira.summary: Two-way sync of compliance tasks and risks with Jira Cloud, including importing risks your team logs in Jira.
/help/jira.body_md:
Many teams live in Jira. The Jira integration puts compliance work where engineers already are, and brings the status back.

## Connecting

**Integrations → Jira → Connect**:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Jira site URL | `https://yourcompany.atlassian.net` |
| Atlassian account email | The account the API token belongs to (a service account is best) |
| API token | Create one at id.atlassian.com under Security → API tokens |
| Project key | The project for compliance issues, for example `SEC` |
| Issue type | For tasks, usually `Task` |
| Sync tasks with priority at least | `low`, `medium` (default) or `high` |
| Create a Jira issue for every new risk | `yes` (default) or `no` |
| Issue type for risks | `Task`, or `Risk` if your project has that type |
| Import risks from Jira matching this JQL | Optional, for example `project = SEC AND labels = risk` |

The account needs permission to create and edit issues in the project.

## Tasks

- Tasks at or above the chosen priority are created as Jira issues on the next sync, with a link back to the platform.
- When the issue is **Done** in Jira, the task is marked done here.
- The task shows the issue key and a link.

## Risks

- **New risks** get a Jira issue as soon as they're saved (when automatic creation is on). The issue contains the summary `[Risk] …`, the description, the score with likelihood and impact, the treatment and plan, linked controls and a link back. Labels `risk`, `pramaanly` and `risk-high`, `risk-medium` or `risk-low` are added.
- **Edits** to a risk are pushed to its issue.
- **Status comes back**: when the issue's status category is **Done**, the risk becomes **Treated**; if the issue is reopened, the risk goes back to **Open**. The Jira status name is shown next to the risk.
- **Import**: issues matching your JQL that aren't already linked are imported as risks (likelihood and impact 3, treatment Mitigate; review and score them), with the assignee as owner where their email matches a member.
- If Jira is slow or down when you save a risk, the risk is still saved and the issue is created on the next sync.

On the **Risk register**, **Sync with Jira** runs a sync immediately, and **Create issue** links a risk added before Jira was connected.

## When it runs

With the other integrations, every 6 hours, and immediately when you click **Run checks** on the integration or **Sync with Jira** on the risk register.

/help/notifications.title: Notifications and alerts
/help/notifications.summary: The emails and Slack or Teams alerts the platform sends, and how to set up channels.
/help/notifications.body_md:
The platform tells people when something needs them, so nobody has to remember to check.

## Channels

Set up in **Settings → Notifications** (admins):

- **Email**: to the person concerned, and to an optional shared address (for example security@yourcompany.com) for organisation-wide alerts;
- **Slack**: an incoming webhook URL (`https://hooks.slack.com/…`);
- **Microsoft Teams**: a Teams or Power Automate workflow webhook URL.

**Send a test** checks each channel. Webhook URLs are encrypted, and only genuine Slack and Microsoft webhook addresses are accepted, so a webhook can't be pointed at an internal service.

## What gets sent

| Event | Who | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Check failed | Control owner or admins, plus Slack/Teams | An integration check starts failing (a Fix: task is created at the same time) |
| Incident reported | Incident followers (reporter, lead, admins), plus Slack/Teams | Immediately, with the clocks that are running |
| Incident updates | Incident followers, except whoever made the change | Updates, status, severity, lead, classification and regulatory reports, all in one email thread per incident. See [Incidents](/docs/incidents#tracking-by-email) |
| Regulatory deadlines | Incident followers, lead and admins; rights request assignee or admins | CERT-In 2 hours before and overdue; Board report 24 hours before and overdue; rights requests 3 days before and overdue |
| Task assigned or created | Assignee (or admins) | When assigned; tasks the platform creates |
| Task due | Assignee | The day before, and when overdue |
| Control assigned | New owner | When you're made owner of controls |
| Evidence to review | Control owner or admins | When someone uploads evidence |
| Evidence sent back | Uploader | With the reviewer's reason |
| Evidence request | Assignee and requester | When a request is raised, commented on, answered and decided |
| Access review | Reviewers | When accounts are assigned to you; before the due date |
| Policy approved | Everyone | When a policy needs reading and acknowledging (new members get one welcome email listing policies to read) |
| Vendor questionnaire | Vendor owner or admins | When a vendor submits, with the score |
| Vendor document expiring | Vendor owner or admins | Before and after expiry |
| Training due | Each person | At most weekly while training is overdue |

Emails link straight to the relevant page. The same event is never sent twice. Emails about one incident are threaded together in your inbox.

## Email setup

Self-hosted installations need an SMTP server (Amazon SES, Postmark, SendGrid or a Google Workspace relay) set in `SMTP_*` variables. Without one, emails are written to the worker log instead. See [Self-hosting](/docs/self-hosting).
